Parallel mode no longer prints an "experimental" banner, and sessions can check
`session.parallel` to see if they run in a parallel worker. A new `rattler`
backend uses py-rattler (install with the `nox[rattler]` extra), so you can
request fast conda-style environments in a `/// script` block. Python versions
read from classifiers now include free-threaded builds when the free-threading
classifier is present, and are deduplicated. A single-argument
`@nox.parametrize` now accepts ranges and other iterators, and the `rattler`
backend loads config from the default locations. The GitHub Action now
defaults to Python 3.11-3.15. This release also fixes several bugs in script

better at finding Python and supports version specifier sets. Using this,
script mode reads `requires-python`. Many bugs were fixed, mostly in Python
version handling, conda version specifiers, and option precedence. Unrecognized
global options are now an error.

**Heads up!** This is a very big release for Nox. Please read these release notes thoroughly and reach out to us on GitHub if you run into issues.
Breaking changes and other important notes:

* Nox is now published as "nox" on PyPI. This means that Nox is installed via `pip install nox` instead of `nox-automation`. Since the new release makes so many breaking changes, we won't be updating the old `nox-automation` package.
* Nox's configuration file is now called `noxfile.py` instead of `nox.py`.
* Nox no longer supports Python 2.7. You can still create and run Python 2.7 sessions, but Nox itself must be installed using Python 3.5+.

* Nox's behavior has been changed from *declarative*  to *imperative*. Session actions now run immediately. Existing code to setup session virtualenv, such as `session.interpreter` **will break**! Please consult the documentation on how to use `@nox.session(python=[...])` to configure virtualenvs for sessions.
* Nox now uses calver for releases.
* Support for the legacy naming convention (for example, `session_tests`) has been removed.
* Fix python syntax error on docs. (#111)
* Use a configuration file for readthedocs. (#107)
* Fix processing of numeric Python versions that specify a patch version.
* Produce better error message when sessions can't be found.
* Make session.install a simple alias for session.run.
* Refactor nox.command.Command as nox.command.run, reducing complexity.
* Add list of projects that use Nox.
**Note**:: v0.19.1 was the last version released as "nox-automation" on PyPI. Subsequent releases are published as "nox".
* Updates copyright information and contact addresses. No code changes.
* Don't skip install commands when reusing existing virtualenvs. (#86)
* Simulating `unittest.mock` backport in the Python 2 standard library. (#81)
* On Windows, use the `py.exe` [launcher][2] (e.g. `py.exe -2.7`) to locate
* Fix Nox not returning a non-zero exit code on failure. (#55)
* Making sure all `Command`s use run in `__call__`. (#48)
* Refactor the list of sessions into a manifest class. (#38)
* Changed some instances of session to be plural (#37)

a different file using the ``--noxfile`` argument when running ``nox``.

You can also configure sessions to run against multiple Python versions as described in :ref:`virtualenv config` and  parametrize sessions as described in :ref:`parametrized sessions <parametrized>`.
By default, all sessions will be run if no sessions are specified. You can
remove sessions from this default list by passing ``default=False`` in the

You can add a description to your session using a `docstring <https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0257>`__.

Modifying Nox's behavior in the Noxfile

Nox has various :doc:`command line arguments <usage>` that can be used to modify its behavior. Some of these can also be specified in the Noxfile using ``nox.options``. For example, if you wanted to store Nox's virtualenvs in a different directory without needing to pass it into ``nox`` every time:
Or, if you wanted to provide a set of sessions that are run by default (this overrides the ``default=`` argument to sessions):
The following options can be specified in the Noxfile:

* ``nox.options.sessions`` is equivalent to specifying :ref:`-s or --sessions <opt-sessions-pythons-and-keywords>`. If set to an empty list, no sessions will be run if no sessions were given on the command line, and the list of available sessions will be shown instead.
* ``nox.options.reuse_venv`` is equivalent to specifying :ref:`--reuse-venv <opt-reuse-venv>`. Preferred over using ``nox.options.reuse_existing_virtualenvs``.

* ``nox.options.reuse_existing_virtualenvs`` is equivalent to specifying :ref:`--reuse-existing-virtualenvs <opt-reuse-existing-virtualenvs>`. You can force this off by specifying ``--no-reuse-existing-virtualenvs`` during invocation. Alias of ``nox.options.reuse_venv=yes|no``.

* ``nox.options.stop_on_first_error`` is equivalent to specifying :ref:`--stop-on-first-error <opt-stop-on-first-error>`. You can force this off by specifying ``--no-stop-on-first-error`` during invocation.

* ``nox.options.error_on_missing_interpreters`` is equivalent to specifying :ref:`--error-on-missing-interpreters <opt-error-on-missing-interpreters>`. You can force this off by specifying ``--no-error-on-missing-interpreters`` during invocation.

* ``nox.options.error_on_external_run`` is equivalent to specifying :ref:`--error-on-external-run <opt-error-on-external-run>`. You can force this off by specifying ``--no-error-on-external-run`` during invocation.
* ``nox.options.allow_parallel`` is equivalent to specifying :ref:`--allow-parallel <opt-allow-parallel>`. You can force this off by specifying ``--no-allow-parallel`` during invocation.
* ``nox.options.verbose`` is equivalent to specifying :ref:`-v or --verbose <opt-verbose>`. You can force this off by specifying ``--no-verbose`` during invocation.

When invoking ``nox``, any options specified on the command line take precedence over the options specified in the Noxfile. If either ``--sessions`` or ``--keywords`` is specified on the command line, *both* options specified in the Noxfile will be ignored.

Parallel execution is opt-in per session: only sessions declared with

Sessions that don't opt in still run under ``--parallel``, but not in parallel.
They start only once nothing else is running, and nothing starts alongside
them. If no selected session opts in, Nox warns and runs sequentially as usual.

``allow_parallel=`` value always wins over the global default, and
``--no-allow-parallel`` on the command line overrides the Noxfile setting.

Nox is not the only tool of its kind. If Nox doesn't quite fit your needs or you want to do more research, we recommend looking at these tools:
- `tox <https://tox.readthedocs.org>`__ is the de-facto standard for managing multiple Python test environments, and is the direct spiritual ancestor to Nox.

- `Invoke <https://www.pyinvoke.org/>`__ is a general-purpose task execution library, similar to Make. Nox can be thought of as if Invoke were tailored specifically to Python testing, so Invoke is a great choice for scripts that need to encompass far more than Nox's specialization.
- `Hatch <https://hatch.pypa.io>`__ A modern, extensible Python project manager using ``pyproject.toml`` configuration and a scripts + environments approach.

Parallel mode no longer prints an "experimental" banner, and sessions can check
`session.parallel` to see if they run in a parallel worker. A new `rattler`
backend uses py-rattler (install with the `nox[rattler]` extra), so you can
request fast conda-style environments in a `/// script` block. Python versions
read from classifiers now include free-threaded builds when the free-threading
classifier is present, and are deduplicated. A single-argument
`@nox.parametrize` now accepts ranges and other iterators, and the `rattler`
backend loads config from the default locations. The GitHub Action now
defaults to Python 3.11-3.15. This release also fixes several bugs in script

**Heads up!** This is a very big release for Nox. Please read these release notes thoroughly and reach out to us on GitHub if you run into issues.
Breaking changes and other important notes:

* Nox is now published as "nox" on PyPI. This means that Nox is installed via `pip install nox` instead of `nox-automation`. Since the new release makes so many breaking changes, we won't be updating the old `nox-automation` package.
* Nox's configuration file is now called `noxfile.py` instead of `nox.py`.
* Nox no longer supports Python 2.7. You can still create and run Python 2.7 sessions, but Nox itself must be installed using Python 3.5+.

* Nox's behavior has been changed from *declarative*  to *imperative*. Session actions now run immediately. Existing code to setup session virtualenv, such as `session.interpreter` **will break**! Please consult the documentation on how to use `@nox.session(python=[...])` to configure virtualenvs for sessions.
* Nox now uses calver for releases.
* Support for the legacy naming convention (for example, `session_tests`) has been removed.
* Fix python syntax error on docs. (#111)
* Use a configuration file for readthedocs. (#107)
* Fix processing of numeric Python versions that specify a patch version.
* Produce better error message when sessions can't be found.
* Make session.install a simple alias for session.run.
* Refactor nox.command.Command as nox.command.run, reducing complexity.
* Add list of projects that use Nox.
**Note**:: v0.19.1 was the last version released as "nox-automation" on PyPI. Subsequent releases are published as "nox".
* Updates copyright information and contact addresses. No code changes.
* Don't skip install commands when reusing existing virtualenvs. (#86)
* Simulating `unittest.mock` backport in the Python 2 standard library. (#81)
* On Windows, use the `py.exe` [launcher][2] (e.g. `py.exe -2.7`) to locate
* Fix Nox not returning a non-zero exit code on failure. (#55)
* Making sure all `Command`s use run in `__call__`. (#48)
* Refactor the list of sessions into a manifest class. (#38)
* Changed some instances of session to be plural (#37)

114|def parse_parallel(value: str | int) -> int:
115|    """Resolve a ``--parallel`` value to a positive integer.
116|
117|    Accepts a positive integer (or its string form) or ``"auto"`` (the CPU
118|    count). Used for command-line, ``NOX_PARALLEL``, and Noxfile-set values.
119|
120|    Raises:
121|        ValueError: If the value is not ``"auto"`` or a positive integer.
122|    """
123|    if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip().lower() == "auto":
124|        return os.cpu_count() or 1
125|    try:
126|        jobs = int(value)
127|    except (TypeError, ValueError):
128|        msg = (
129|            f"invalid parallel value {value!r} (expected a positive integer or 'auto')"
130|        )
131|        raise ValueError(msg) from None
132|    if jobs < 1:
133|        msg = f"parallel value must be >= 1, got {jobs}"
134|        raise ValueError(msg)
135|    return jobs
136|
137|
138|def _parallel_converter(value: str | int | None) -> int | None:
139|    """Normalize ``parallel`` however it arrives (CLI, env var, or Noxfile)."""
140|    return None if value is None else parse_parallel(value)
141|
142|
143|def _parallel_arg(value: str) -> int:
144|    """``argparse`` type for ``--parallel`` that reports errors nicely."""
145|    try:
146|        return parse_parallel(value)
147|    except ValueError as exc:
148|        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(str(exc)) from None

90|def _chdir(path: str) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
91|    """
92|    Change the current working directory to the given path.
93|    Follows python 3.11's chdir behaviour.
94|    """

98|        yield
99|    finally:

103|def _normalize_path(envdir: str, path: str) -> str:
104|    """Normalizes a string to be a "safe" filesystem path for a virtualenv."""
105|    orig_path = path
106|    path = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", path).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
107|    path = re.sub(r"[^\w\s-]", "-", path).strip().lower()
108|    path = re.sub(r"[-\s]+", "-", path)
109|    path = path.strip("-")
110|
111|    if not path:
112|        path = hashlib.sha1(orig_path.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]  # noqa: S324
113|        logger.warning(
114|            "The virtualenv name was hashed because it contains no usable "
115|            "ASCII characters."
116|        )
117|
118|    full_path = os.path.join(envdir, path)
119|    if len(full_path) > 100 - len("bin/pythonX.Y"):
120|        if len(envdir) < 100 - 9:
121|            path = hashlib.sha1(path.encode("ascii")).hexdigest()[:8]  # noqa: S324
122|            full_path = os.path.join(envdir, path)
123|            logger.warning("The virtualenv name was hashed to avoid being too long.")
124|        else:
125|            logger.error(
126|                f"The virtualenv path {full_path} is too long and will cause issues on "
127|                "some environments. Use the --envdir path to modify where "
128|                "Nox stores virtualenvs."
129|            )
130|
131|    return full_path

398|    def run(
399|        self,
400|        *args: str | os.PathLike[str],
401|        env: Mapping[str, str | None] | None = None,
402|        include_outer_env: bool = True,
403|        silent: bool = False,
404|        success_codes: Iterable[int] | None = None,
405|        log: bool = True,
406|        external: ExternalType | None = None,
407|        stdout: int | IO[str] | None = None,
408|        stderr: int | IO[str] | None = subprocess.STDOUT,
409|        interrupt_timeout: float | None = DEFAULT_INTERRUPT_TIMEOUT,
410|        terminate_timeout: float | None = DEFAULT_TERMINATE_TIMEOUT,
411|    ) -> str | bool | None:
412|        """Run a command.
413|
414|        Commands must be specified as a list of strings, for example::
415|
416|            session.run('pytest', '-k', 'fast', 'tests/')
417|            session.run('flake8', '--import-order-style=google')
418|
419|        You **can not** just pass everything as one string. For example, this
420|        **will not work**::
421|
422|            session.run('pytest -k fast tests/')
423|
424|        You can set environment variables for the command using ``env``::
425|
426|            session.run(
427|                'bash', '-c', 'echo $SOME_ENV',
428|                env={'SOME_ENV': 'Hello'})
429|
430|        You can extend the shutdown timeout to allow long-running cleanup tasks to
431|        complete before being terminated. For example, if you wanted to allow ``pytest``
432|        extra time to clean up large projects in the case that Nox receives an
433|        interrupt signal from your build system and needs to terminate its child
434|        processes::
435|
436|            session.run(
437|                'pytest', '-k', 'long_cleanup',
438|                interrupt_timeout=10.0,
439|                terminate_timeout=2.0)
440|
441|        You can also tell Nox to treat non-zero exit codes as success using
442|        ``success_codes``. For example, if you wanted to treat the ``pytest``
443|        "tests discovered, but none selected" error as success::
444|
445|            session.run(
446|                'pytest', '-k', 'not slow',
447|                success_codes=[0, 5])
448|
449|        On Windows, builtin commands like ``del`` cannot be directly invoked,
450|        but you can use ``cmd /c`` to invoke them::
451|
452|            session.run('cmd', '/c', 'del', 'docs/modules.rst')
453|
454|        If ``session.run`` fails, it will stop the session and will not run the next steps.
455|        Basically, this will raise a Python exception. Taking this in count, you can use a
456|        ``try...finally`` block for cleanup runs, that will run even if the other runs fail::
457|
458|           try:
459|               session.run("coverage", "run", "-m", "pytest")
460|           finally:
461|               # Display coverage report even when tests fail.
462|               session.run("coverage", "report")
463|
464|        If you pass ``silent=True``, you can capture the output of a command that would
465|        otherwise be shown to the user. For example to get the current Git commit ID::
466|
467|            out = session.run(
468|                "git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD",
469|                external=True, silent=True
470|            )
471|
472|            print("Current Git commit is", out.strip())
473|
474|        :param env: A dictionary of environment variables to expose to the
475|            command. By default, all environment variables are passed. You
476|            can block an environment variable from the outer environment by
477|            setting it to None.
478|        :type env: dict or None
479|        :param include_outer_env: Boolean parameter that determines if the
480|            environment variables from the nox invocation environment should
481|            be passed to the command. ``True`` by default.
482|        :type include_outer_env: bool
483|        :param bool silent: Silence command output, unless the command fails.
484|            If ``True``, returns the command output (unless the command fails).
485|            ``False`` by default.
486|        :param success_codes: A list of return codes that are considered
487|            successful. By default, only ``0`` is considered success.
488|        :type success_codes: list, tuple, or None
489|        :param external: If False (the default) then programs not in the
490|            virtualenv path will cause a warning. If True, no warning will be
491|            emitted. These warnings can be turned into errors using
492|            ``--error-on-external-run``. This has no effect for sessions that
493|            do not have a virtualenv.
494|        :type external: bool
495|        :param interrupt_timeout: The timeout (in seconds) that Nox should wait after it
496|            and its children receive an interrupt signal before sending a terminate
497|            signal to its children. Set to ``None`` to never send a terminate signal.
498|            Default: ``0.3``
499|        :type interrupt_timeout: float or None
500|        :param terminate_timeout: The timeout (in seconds) that Nox should wait after it
501|            sends a terminate signal to its children before sending a kill signal to
502|            them. Set to ``None`` to never send a kill signal.
503|            Default: ``0.2``
504|        :type terminate_timeout: float or None
505|        :param stdout: Redirect standard output of the command into a file. Can't be
506|            combined with *silent*.
507|        :type stdout: file or file descriptor
508|        :param stderr: Redirect standard output of the command into a file. Can't be
509|            combined with *silent*.
510|        :type stderr: file or file descriptor
511|        """
512|        if not args:
513|            msg = "At least one argument required to run()."
514|            raise ValueError(msg)
515|
516|        if len(args) == 1 and isinstance(args[0], (list, tuple)):
517|            msg = "First argument to `session.run` is a list. Did you mean to use `session.run(*args)`?"
518|            raise ValueError(msg)
519|
520|        if self._runner.global_config.install_only:
521|            logger.info(f"Skipping {args[0]} run, as --install-only is set.")
522|            return None
523|
524|        return self._run(
525|            *args,
526|            env=env,
527|            include_outer_env=include_outer_env,
528|            silent=silent,
529|            success_codes=success_codes,
530|            log=log,
531|            external=external,
532|            stdout=stdout,
533|            stderr=stderr,
534|            interrupt_timeout=interrupt_timeout,
535|            terminate_timeout=terminate_timeout,
536|        )

654|    def _run(
655|        self,
656|        *args: str | os.PathLike[str],
657|        env: Mapping[str, str | None] | None = None,
658|        include_outer_env: bool,
659|        silent: bool,
660|        success_codes: Iterable[int] | None,
661|        log: bool,
662|        external: ExternalType | None,
663|        stdout: int | IO[str] | None,
664|        stderr: int | IO[str] | None,
665|        interrupt_timeout: float | None,
666|        terminate_timeout: float | None,
667|    ) -> str | bool:
668|        """Like run(), except that it runs even if --install-only is provided."""
669|        # Legacy support - run a function given.
670|        if callable(args[0]):
671|            return self._run_func(args[0], args[1:])  # type: ignore[unreachable]
672|
673|        # Using `"uv"` or `"uvx" when `uv` is the backend is guaranteed to
674|        # work, even if it was co-installed with nox.
675|        if self.virtualenv.venv_backend == "uv" and nox.virtualenv.UV != "uv":
676|            if (
677|                args[0] == "uv"
678|                and shutil.which("uv", path=self.bin)
679|                is None  # Session uv takes priority
680|            ):
681|                args = (nox.virtualenv.UV, *args[1:])
682|            elif args[0] == "uvx" and shutil.which("uvx", path=self.bin) is None:
683|                args = (f"{nox.virtualenv.UV}x", *args[1:])
684|
685|        # Combine the env argument with our virtualenv's env vars.

930|    def notify(

941|        from a test session::

946|                session.notify("coverage")

948|            @nox.session
949|            def coverage(session):
950|                session.run("coverage")

956|                Passing the decorated function object is not currently
957|                supported.

959|                arguments *only* for the queued session. Otherwise, the
960|                standard globally available positional arguments will be
961|                used instead.

963|        Raises:
964|            ValueError: If called under ``--no-dependencies`` (which includes
965|                every session run by ``--parallel``): the notified session

967|                racing on its virtualenv. Use ``requires=`` instead.

969|        if self._runner.global_config.no_dependencies:
970|            msg = (
971|                "session.notify() is not supported with --no-dependencies (which"

1029|def resolve_reuse_existing_venv(global_config: NoxConfig, func: Func) -> bool:
1030|    """Determines whether to reuse an existing virtual environment.
1031|
1032|    The decision matrix is as follows:
1033|
1034|    +--------------------------+-----------------+-------------+
1035|    | global_config.reuse_venv | func.reuse_venv | Reuse venv? |
1036|    +==========================+=================+=============+
1037|    | "always"                 | N/A             | Yes         |
1038|    +--------------------------+-----------------+-------------+
1039|    | "never"                  | N/A             | No          |
1040|    +--------------------------+-----------------+-------------+
1041|    | "yes"                    | True|None       | Yes         |
1042|    +--------------------------+-----------------+-------------+
1043|    | "yes"                    | False           | No          |
1044|    +--------------------------+-----------------+-------------+
1045|    | "no"                     | True            | Yes         |
1046|    +--------------------------+-----------------+-------------+
1047|    | "no"                     | False|None      | No          |
1048|    +--------------------------+-----------------+-------------+
1049|
1050|    Summary
1051|    ~~~~~~~
1052|    - "always" forces reuse regardless of `func.reuse_venv`.
1053|    - "never" forces recreation regardless of `func.reuse_venv`.
1054|    - "yes" and "no" respect `func.reuse_venv` being ``False`` or ``True`` respectively.
1055|    """
1056|    return any(
1057|        (
1058|            # "always" forces reuse regardless of func.reuse_venv
1059|            global_config.reuse_venv == "always",
1060|            # Respect func.reuse_venv when it's explicitly True, unless global_config is "never"
1061|            func.reuse_venv is True and global_config.reuse_venv != "never",
1062|            # Delegate to reuse ("yes") when func.reuse_venv is not explicitly False
1063|            func.reuse_venv is not False and global_config.reuse_venv == "yes",
1064|        )
1065|    )

1311|            session,
1312|            Status.ABORTED,
1313|            reason=(
1314|                f"Prerequisite session {dependency.friendly_name} was not successful"
1315|            ),
1316|            duration=0,
1317|        )
1318|
1319|    @property
1320|    def imperfect(self) -> str:
1321|        """Return the English imperfect tense for the status.
1322|
1323|        Returns:
1324|            str: A word or phrase representing the status.
1325|        """
1326|        match self.status:
1327|            case Status.SUCCESS:
1328|                return "was successful" + _duration_str(self.duration, " in {time}")
1329|            case _:
1330|                status = self.status.name.lower()
1331|                if self.reason:
1332|                    duration_err = _duration_str(self.duration, " (took {time})")
1333|                    return f"{status}: {self.reason}{duration_err}"
1334|                return status
1335|
1336|    def log(self, message: str) -> None:
1337|        """Log a message using the appropriate log function.
1338|
1339|        Args:
1340|            message (str): The message to be logged.
1341|        """
1342|        match self.status:
1343|            case Status.SUCCESS:
1344|                log_function = logger.success
1345|            case Status.SKIPPED:
1346|                log_function = logger.warning
1347|            case status:
1348|                log_function = logger.error if status.value <= 0 else logger.info
1349|        log_function(message)
1350|
1351|    def serialize(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
1352|        """Return a serialized representation of this result.
1353|
1354|        Returns:
1355|            dict: The serialized result.
1356|        """
1357|        return {
1358|            "args": getattr(self.session.func, "call_spec", {}),
1359|            "name": self.session.name,
1360|            "result": self.status.name.lower(),
1361|            "result_code": self.status.value,
1362|            "reason": self.reason,
1363|            "signatures": self.session.signatures,
1364|            "duration": self.duration,
1365|        }
1366|
1367|    @classmethod
1368|    def from_dict(cls, session: SessionRunner, entry: dict[str, Any]) -> Result:
1369|        """Rebuild a result from a :meth:`serialize` entry."""
1370|        return cls(
1371|            session,
1372|            Status[entry["result"].upper()],
1373|            entry.get("reason"),
1374|            duration=entry.get("duration", 0.0),
1375|        )

71|def session_decorator(
72|    func: Callable[..., Any] | Func | None = None,
73|    /,
74|    python: Python | None = None,
75|    py: Python | None = None,
76|    reuse_venv: bool | None = None,  # noqa: FBT001
77|    name: str | None = None,
78|    venv_backend: str | None = None,
79|    venv_params: Sequence[str] = (),
80|    tags: Sequence[str] | None = None,
81|    *,
82|    default: bool = True,
83|    requires: Sequence[str] | None = None,
84|    download_python: Literal["auto", "never", "always"] | None = None,
85|    allow_parallel: bool | None = None,
86|) -> Func | Callable[[RawFunc | Func], Func]:
87|    """Designate the decorated function as a session."""
88|    # If `func` is provided, then this is the decorator call with the function
89|    # being sent as part of the Python syntax (`@nox.session`).
90|    # If `func` is None, however, then this is a plain function call, and it
91|    # must return the decorator that ultimately is applied
92|    # (`@nox.session(...)`).
93|    #
94|    # This is what makes the syntax with and without parentheses both work.
95|    if func is None:
96|        return functools.partial(
97|            session_decorator,
98|            python=python,
99|            py=py,
100|            reuse_venv=reuse_venv,
101|            name=name,
102|            venv_backend=venv_backend,
103|            venv_params=venv_params,
104|            tags=tags,
105|            default=default,
106|            requires=requires,
107|            download_python=download_python,
108|            allow_parallel=allow_parallel,
109|        )
110|
111|    if isinstance(func, Func):
112|        func = func.func
113|
114|    if py is not None and python is not None:
115|        msg = (
116|            "The py argument to nox.session is an alias for the python "
117|            "argument, please only specify one."
118|        )
119|        raise ValueError(msg)
120|
121|    if python is None:
122|        python = py
123|
124|    reg_name = name or func.__name__
125|
126|    fn = Func(
127|        func,
128|        python,
129|        reuse_venv,
130|        reg_name,
131|        venv_backend,
132|        venv_params,
133|        tags=tags,
134|        default=default,
135|        requires=requires,
136|        download_python=download_python,
137|        allow_parallel=allow_parallel,
138|    )
139|    if reg_name in _REGISTRY:
140|        msg = (
141|            f"The session {reg_name!r} has already been registered; "
142|            "this will be an error in a future version of nox. "
143|            "Overriding the old session for now."
144|        )
145|        warnings.warn(msg, FutureWarning, stacklevel=2)
146|    _REGISTRY[reg_name] = fn
147|    return fn

96|def get_dependencies(
97|    req: packaging.requirements.Requirement,
98|) -> Iterator[packaging.requirements.Requirement]:
99|    """
100|    Gets all dependencies. Raises ModuleNotFoundError if a package is not installed.
101|    """
102|    seen: set[tuple[packaging.utils.NormalizedName, frozenset[str]]] = set()
103|
104|    def expand(
105|        req: packaging.requirements.Requirement,
106|    ) -> Iterator[packaging.requirements.Requirement]:
107|        # Skip the metadata read and re-expansion for requirements already
108|        # visited with the same extras; this avoids rescanning shared
109|        # dependencies reachable through multiple extras and guards against
110|        # dependency cycles. The requirement itself is still yielded so that
111|        # every specifier is checked downstream.
112|        key = (packaging.utils.canonicalize_name(req.name), frozenset(req.extras))
113|        if key in seen:
114|            yield req
115|            return
116|        seen.add(key)
117|
118|        info = importlib.metadata.metadata(req.name)
119|        yield req
120|
121|        dist_list = info.get_all("requires-dist") or []
122|        extra_list = [packaging.requirements.Requirement(mk) for mk in dist_list]
123|        # "" is the base install (no extra)
124|        wanted_extras = {"", *req.extras}
125|        for ireq in extra_list:
126|            if ireq.marker and not any(
127|                ireq.marker.evaluate({"extra": extra}) for extra in wanted_extras
128|            ):
129|                continue
130|            yield from expand(ireq)
131|
132|    yield from expand(req)

135|def check_dependencies(dependencies: list[str]) -> bool:
136|    """
137|    Checks to see if a list of dependencies is currently installed.
138|    """
139|    itr_deps = (packaging.requirements.Requirement(d) for d in dependencies)
140|    deps = [d for d in itr_deps if not d.marker or d.marker.evaluate()]
141|
142|    # Select the one nox dependency (required)
143|    nox_dep = [d for d in deps if packaging.utils.canonicalize_name(d.name) == "nox"]
144|    if not nox_dep:
145|        msg = "Must have a nox dependency in TOML script dependencies"
146|        raise ValueError(msg)
147|
148|    try:
149|        expanded_deps = {d for req in deps for d in get_dependencies(req)}
150|    except ModuleNotFoundError:
151|        return False
152|
153|    for dep in expanded_deps:
154|        if dep.specifier:
155|            version = importlib.metadata.version(dep.name)
156|            if not dep.specifier.contains(version):
157|                return False
158|        if dep.url:
159|            dist = importlib.metadata.distribution(dep.name)
160|            if not check_url_dependency(dep.url, dist):
161|                return False
162|
163|    return True

166|def check_requires_python(requires_python: str | None, version: str) -> bool:
167|    """
168|    Checks a Python version like ``"3.12.1"`` against a ``requires-python``
169|    specifier set. True if no specifier is given.
170|    """
171|    if not requires_python:
172|        return True
173|    try:
174|        specifiers = packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet(requires_python)
175|    except packaging.specifiers.InvalidSpecifier as err:
176|        msg = f'Invalid "requires-python": {requires_python!r} ({err})'
177|        raise SystemExit(msg) from err
178|    # prereleases=True so a prerelease interpreter still matches plain specs
179|    # like ">=3.9"; PEP 440 ordering (beta < final) still applies.
180|    return specifiers.contains(version, prereleases=True)

183|def _format_python_version(version_info: tuple[int, int, int, str, int]) -> str:
184|    # For the running interpreter, pass sys.version_info[:5] rather than
185|    # platform.python_version(), which can produce unparsable values like
186|    # "3.13.0+" on dev builds.
187|    major, minor, micro, releaselevel, serial = version_info
188|    pre = {"alpha": "a", "beta": "b", "candidate": "rc"}.get(releaselevel, "")
189|    suffix = f"{pre}{serial}" if pre else ""
190|    return f"{major}.{minor}.{micro}{suffix}"

193|def _venv_python_version(venv: nox.virtualenv.ProcessEnv) -> str | None:
194|    """The environment's Python version as PEP 440, or None if it can't run."""
195|    python_cmd = shutil.which("python", path=venv._get_env({}).get("PATH"))
196|    if python_cmd is None:
197|        return None
198|    from python_discovery import PythonInfo  # noqa: PLC0415
199|
200|    cache = nox.virtualenv._get_python_discovery_cache()
201|    try:
202|        info = PythonInfo.from_exe(python_cmd, cache=cache, raise_on_error=False)
203|    except OSError:
204|        # The cache dir exists but isn't writable; probe without it.
205|        info = PythonInfo.from_exe(python_cmd, raise_on_error=False)
206|    if info is not None:
207|        return _format_python_version(info.version_info)
208|    # Discovery can fail to introspect an interpreter that still runs fine
209|    # (e.g. restricted filesystem permissions); ask the interpreter directly.
210|    cmd = [python_cmd, "-c", "import sys; print(*sys.version_info[:5])"]
211|    try:
212|        out = subprocess.run(
213|            cmd, check=True, capture_output=True, encoding="utf-8"
214|        ).stdout
215|        major, minor, micro, releaselevel, serial = out.split()
216|        version_info = (int(major), int(minor), int(micro), releaselevel, int(serial))
217|    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError, ValueError):
218|        return None
219|    return _format_python_version(version_info)

222|def check_url_dependency(dep_url: str, dist: importlib.metadata.Distribution) -> bool:
223|    """
224|    Check to see if a url matches an installed distribution object. Returns false if
225|    this is not a clear match.
226|    """
227|
228|    # The .origin property added in Python 3.13
229|    origin = getattr(dist, "origin", None)
230|    if origin is None:
231|        return False
232|
233|    dep_purl = urllib.parse.urlparse(dep_url)
234|
235|    if hasattr(origin, "requested_revision"):
236|        origin_purl = urllib.parse.urlparse(f"{origin.url}@{origin.requested_revision}")
237|    else:
238|        origin_purl = urllib.parse.urlparse(origin.url)
239|
240|    return dep_purl.netloc == origin_purl.netloc and dep_purl.path == origin_purl.path

279|def run_script_mode(
280|    noxfile: str,
281|    envdir: Path,
282|    *,
283|    reuse: bool,
284|    dependencies: list[str],
285|    venv_backend: str,
286|    download_python: Literal["auto", "never", "always"],
287|    requires_python: str | None,
288|) -> NoReturn:
289|    envdir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
290|    noxenv = envdir.joinpath("_nox_script_mode")
291|
292|    venv = _make_env(
293|        noxenv,
294|        reuse_existing=reuse,
295|        venv_backend=venv_backend,
296|        download_python=download_python,
297|        requires_python=requires_python,
298|    )
299|    if requires_python:
300|        if not venv.is_sandboxed:
301|            version = _format_python_version(sys.version_info[:5])
302|            if not check_requires_python(requires_python, version):
303|                msg = (
304|                    f'Python {version} does not satisfy "requires-python":'
305|                    f' {requires_python!r}, and the "none" script backend cannot'
306|                    " switch interpreters"
307|                )
308|                raise SystemExit(msg)
309|        else:
310|            env_version = _venv_python_version(venv)
311|            satisfied = env_version is not None and check_requires_python(
312|                requires_python, env_version
313|            )
314|            if not satisfied and venv._reused:
315|                # A reused environment may predate a requires-python change;
316|                # its interpreter spec is not resolved on the reuse path.
317|                logger.info(
318|                    "Recreating script environment: its Python"
319|                    f" ({env_version or 'unknown'}) does not satisfy"
320|                    f' "requires-python": {requires_python!r}'
321|                )
322|                venv = _make_env(
323|                    noxenv,
324|                    reuse_existing=False,
325|                    venv_backend=venv_backend,
326|                    download_python=download_python,
327|                    requires_python=requires_python,
328|                )
329|                env_version = _venv_python_version(venv)
330|                satisfied = env_version is not None and check_requires_python(
331|                    requires_python, env_version
332|                )
333|            if not satisfied:
334|                # E.g. a downloaded fallback interpreter can miss the range.
335|                msg = (
336|                    f"Script environment Python ({env_version or 'unknown'})"
337|                    f' does not satisfy "requires-python": {requires_python!r}'
338|                )
339|                raise SystemExit(msg)
340|    # An outer PYTHONPATH can make the installer and the child Nox process load
341|    # packages from outside the script environment instead of its dependencies.
342|    # Stash it so the child can restore it for sessions, which must see the
343|    # same environment as a NOX_SCRIPT_MODE=none run.
344|    env_overrides: dict[str, str | None] = {}
345|    if venv.is_sandboxed:
346|        env_overrides["PYTHONPATH"] = None
347|        outer_pythonpath = os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH")
348|        if outer_pythonpath is not None:
349|            env_overrides["NOX_OUTER_PYTHONPATH"] = outer_pythonpath
350|    env = {k: v for k, v in venv._get_env(env_overrides).items() if v is not None}
351|    env["NOX_SCRIPT_MODE"] = "none"
352|    if venv.venv_backend == "uv":
353|        cmd = [nox.virtualenv.UV, "pip", "install"]
354|    else:
355|        # On Windows, subprocess resolves the executable against the parent
356|        # process's PATH, not the child env's, so resolve pip explicitly.
357|        pip_cmd = shutil.which("pip", path=env["PATH"])
358|        assert pip_cmd is not None, "pip must be discoverable in the environment"
359|        cmd = [pip_cmd, "install"]
360|    subprocess.run([*cmd, *dependencies], env=env, check=True)
361|    nox_cmd = shutil.which("nox", path=env["PATH"])
362|    assert nox_cmd is not None, "Nox must be discoverable when installed"
363|    args = [nox_cmd, "-f", noxfile, *sys.argv[1:]]
364|    # The os.exec functions don't work properly on Windows
365|    if sys.platform.startswith("win"):
366|        raise SystemExit(
367|            subprocess.run(
368|                args,
369|                env=env,
370|                stdout=None,
371|                stderr=None,
372|                encoding="utf-8",
373|                text=True,
374|                check=False,
375|            ).returncode
376|        )
377|    os.execle(nox_cmd, *args, env)  # pragma: nocover # noqa: S606

447|                    )
448|                    or args.download_python
449|                    or "auto"

54|# Note: the implementation (including this regex) taken from PEP 723
55|# https://peps.python.org/pep-0723
56|
57|REGEX = re.compile(
58|    r"(?m)^# /// (?P<type>[a-zA-Z0-9-]+)$\s(?P<content>(^#(| .*)$\s)+)^# ///$"
59|)

62|def load_toml(
63|    filename: os.PathLike[str] | str = "pyproject.toml", *, missing_ok: bool = False
64|) -> dict[str, Any]:
65|    """
66|    Load a toml file or a script with a PEP 723 script block.
67|
68|    The file must have a ``.toml`` extension to be considered a toml file or a
69|    ``.py`` extension / no extension to be considered a script. Other file
70|    extensions are not valid in this function. The default is ``"pyproject.toml"``.
71|
72|    If ``missing_ok``, this will return an empty dict if a script block was not
73|    found, otherwise it will raise a error.
74|
75|    Example:
76|
77|    .. code-block:: python
78|
79|        @nox.session
80|        def myscript(session):
81|            myscript_options = nox.project.load_toml("myscript.py")
82|            session.install(*myscript_options["dependencies"])
83|    """
84|    filepath = Path(filename)
85|    match filepath.suffix:
86|        case ".toml":
87|            return _load_toml_file(filepath)
88|        case ".py" | "":
89|            return _load_script_block(filepath, missing_ok=missing_ok)
90|        case suffix:
91|            msg = f"Extension must be .py or .toml, got {suffix}"
92|            raise ValueError(msg)
93|
94|
95|def _load_toml_file(filepath: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
96|    with filepath.open("rb") as f:
97|        return tomllib.load(f)
98|
99|
100|def _load_script_block(filepath: Path, *, missing_ok: bool) -> dict[str, Any]:
101|    name = "script"
102|    try:
103|        # Decode like Python does, skipping a UTF-8 BOM that would hide a block on the first line.
104|        script = filepath.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
105|    except FileNotFoundError:
106|        if missing_ok:
107|            return {}
108|        raise
109|    matches = [m for m in REGEX.finditer(script) if m.group("type") == name]
110|
111|    if not matches:
112|        if missing_ok:
113|            return {}
114|        msg = f"No {name} block found in {filepath}"
115|        raise ValueError(msg)
116|    if len(matches) > 1:
117|        msg = f"Multiple {name} blocks found in {filepath}"
118|        raise ValueError(msg)
119|
120|    content = "".join(
121|        line[2:] if line.startswith("# ") else line[1:]
122|        for line in matches[0].group("content").splitlines(keepends=True)
123|    )
124|    return tomllib.loads(content)

127|def python_versions(
128|    pyproject: dict[str, Any],
129|    *,
130|    max_version: str | None = None,
131|    sort: bool = True,
132|    free_threaded: bool | None = None,
133|) -> list[str]:
134|    """
135|    Read a list of supported Python versions. Without ``max_version``, this
136|    will read the trove classifiers (recommended). With a ``max_version``, it
137|    will read the requires-python setting for a lower bound, and will use the
138|    value of ``max_version`` as the upper bound. (Reminder: you should never
139|    set an upper bound in ``requires-python``).
140|
141|    Classifier-derived versions are sorted by default. Set ``sort=False`` to
142|    preserve classifier order.
143|
144|    If the project has a ``Programming Language :: Python :: Free Threading``
145|    classifier, free-threaded versions (like ``"3.14t"``) are appended for
146|    every version from 3.14 on. 3.13t is not included, as it was experimental.
147|    Set ``free_threaded`` to force this on or off.
148|
149|    Example:
150|
151|    .. code-block:: python
152|
153|        import nox
154|
155|        PYPROJECT = nox.project.load_toml("pyproject.toml")
156|        # From classifiers
157|        PYTHON_VERSIONS = nox.project.python_versions(PYPROJECT)
158|        # Or from requires-python
159|        PYTHON_VERSIONS = nox.project.python_versions(PYPROJECT, max_version="3.13")
160|    """
161|    classifiers = pyproject.get("project", {}).get("classifiers", [])
162|    if free_threaded is None:
163|        free_threaded = any(
164|            c.startswith("Programming Language :: Python :: Free Threading")
165|            for c in classifiers
166|        )
167|
168|    if max_version is None:
169|        # Classifiers are a list of every Python version
170|        from_classifiers = [
171|            c.split()[-1]
172|            for c in classifiers
173|            if c.startswith("Programming Language :: Python :: 3.")
174|        ]
175|        if not from_classifiers:
176|            msg = 'No Python version classifiers found in "project.classifiers"'
177|            raise ValueError(msg)
178|        if sort:
179|            from_classifiers = sorted(from_classifiers, key=packaging.version.Version)
180|        return _with_free_threaded(from_classifiers, free_threaded=free_threaded)
181|
182|    requires_python_str = pyproject.get("project", {}).get("requires-python", "")
183|    if not requires_python_str:
184|        msg = 'No "project.requires-python" value set'
185|        raise ValueError(msg)
186|
187|    lower_bounds = [
188|        int(spec.version.split(".")[1]) if "." in spec.version else 0
189|        for spec in packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet(requires_python_str)
190|        if spec.operator in {">", ">=", "~="}
191|    ]
192|    if not lower_bounds:
193|        msg = 'No minimum version found in "project.requires-python"'
194|        raise ValueError(msg)
195|    min_minor_version = max(lower_bounds)
196|
197|    max_minor_version = int(max_version.split(".")[1]) if "." in max_version else 0
198|
199|    versions = [f"3.{v}" for v in range(min_minor_version, max_minor_version + 1)]
200|    return _with_free_threaded(versions, free_threaded=free_threaded)
201|
202|
203|def _with_free_threaded(versions: list[str], *, free_threaded: bool) -> list[str]:
204|    if not free_threaded:
205|        return versions
206|    return versions + [
207|        f"{v}t"
208|        for v in versions
209|        if packaging.version.Version(v) >= packaging.version.Version("3.14")
210|    ]

34|class Param:
35|    """A class that encapsulates a single set of parameters to a parametrized
36|    session.
37|
38|    Args:
39|        args (List[Any]): The list of args to pass to the invoked function.
40|        arg_names (Sequence[str]): The names of the args.
41|        id (str): An optional ID for this set of parameters. If unspecified,
42|            it will be generated from the parameters.
43|        tags (Sequence[str]): Optional tags to associate with this set of
44|            parameters.
45|    """
46|
47|    def __init__(
48|        self,
49|        *args: Any,
50|        arg_names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
51|        id: str | None = None,
52|        tags: Sequence[str] | None = None,
53|    ) -> None:
54|        self.args = args
55|        self.id = id
56|
57|        if arg_names is None:
58|            arg_names = ()
59|
60|        self.arg_names = tuple(arg_names)
61|
62|        if tags is None:
63|            tags = []
64|
65|        self.tags = list(tags)
66|
67|    @property
68|    def call_spec(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
69|        return dict(zip(self.arg_names, self.args, strict=True))
70|
71|    def __str__(self) -> str:
72|        if self.id:
73|            return self.id
74|        return ", ".join(f"{k}={v!r}" for k, v in self.call_spec.items())
75|
76|    __repr__ = __str__
77|    __hash__ = None  # type: ignore[assignment]
78|
79|    def copy(self) -> Param:
80|        return self.__class__(
81|            *self.args, arg_names=self.arg_names, id=self.id, tags=self.tags
82|        )
83|
84|    def update(self, other: Param) -> None:
85|        self.id = ", ".join([str(self), str(other)])
86|        self.args += other.args
87|        self.arg_names += other.arg_names
88|        self.tags += other.tags
89|
90|    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
91|        if isinstance(other, self.__class__):
92|            return (
93|                self.args == other.args
94|                and self.arg_names == other.arg_names
95|                and self.id == other.id
96|                and self.tags == other.tags
97|            )
98|        if isinstance(other, dict):
99|            return dict(zip(self.arg_names, self.args, strict=True)) == other
100|
101|        return NotImplemented
102|
103|
104|def _apply_param_specs(param_specs: Iterable[Param], f: Any) -> Any:
105|    previous_param_specs = getattr(f, "parametrize", None)
106|    new_param_specs = update_param_specs(previous_param_specs, param_specs)
107|    f.parametrize = new_param_specs
108|    return f

111|ArgValue = Param | Iterable[Any]
112|
113|
114|def parametrize_decorator(
115|    arg_names: str | Sequence[str],
116|    arg_values_list: Iterable[ArgValue] | ArgValue,
117|    ids: Iterable[str | None] | None = None,
118|    tags: Iterable[Sequence[str]] | None = None,
119|) -> Callable[[Any], Any]:
120|    """Parametrize a session.
121|
122|    Add new invocations to the underlying session function using the list of
123|    ``arg_values_list`` for the given ``arg_names``. Parametrization is
124|    performed during session discovery and each invocation appears as a
125|    separate session to Nox.
126|
127|    Args:
128|        arg_names (Sequence[str]): A list of argument names.
129|        arg_values_list (Iterable[Any] | Any): The list of argument
130|            values determines how often a session is invoked with different
131|            argument values. If only one argument name was specified then
132|            this is a simple list of values, for example ``[1, 2, 3]``. A
133|            list, tuple, range, or iterator (such as a generator) is expanded;
134|            any other value is used as a single value. If N
135|            argument names were specified, this must be a list of N-tuples,
136|            where each tuple-element specifies a value for its respective
137|            argument name, for example ``[(1, 'a'), (2, 'b')]``.
138|        ids (Sequence[str]): Optional sequence of test IDs to use for the
139|            parametrized arguments.
140|        tags (Iterable[Sequence[str]]): Optional iterable of tags to associate
141|            with the parametrized arguments.
142|    """
143|
144|    # Allow args names to be specified as any of 'arg', 'arg,arg2' or ('arg', 'arg2')
145|    if isinstance(arg_names, str):
146|        arg_names = list(filter(None, [arg.strip() for arg in arg_names.split(",")]))
147|
148|    # If there's only one arg_name, arg_values_list should be a single item
149|    # or list. Transform it so it'll work with the combine step.
150|    _arg_values_list: list[Param | Iterable[Any | ArgValue]] = []
151|    if len(arg_names) == 1:
152|        # In this case, the arg_values_list can also just be a single item.
153|        # Must be mutable for the transformation steps
154|        if isinstance(arg_values_list, (list, tuple, range, Iterator)):
155|            _arg_values_list = list[Any](arg_values_list)
156|        else:
157|            _arg_values_list = [arg_values_list]
158|
159|        for n, value in enumerate(_arg_values_list):
160|            if not isinstance(value, Param):
161|                _arg_values_list[n] = [value]
162|    elif isinstance(arg_values_list, Param):
163|        _arg_values_list = [arg_values_list]
164|    else:
165|        _arg_values_list = list(arg_values_list)
166|
167|    # if ids aren't specified at all, make them an empty list for zip.
168|    if not ids:
169|        ids = []
170|
171|    if tags is None:
172|        tags = []
173|
174|    # Generate params for each item in the param_args_values list.
175|    param_specs: list[Param] = []
176|    for param_arg_values, param_id, param_tags in itertools.zip_longest(
177|        _arg_values_list, ids, tags
178|    ):
179|        if isinstance(param_arg_values, Param):
180|            param_spec = param_arg_values
181|            param_spec.arg_names = tuple(arg_names)
182|        else:
183|            param_spec = Param(
184|                *param_arg_values, arg_names=arg_names, id=param_id, tags=param_tags
185|            )
186|
187|        param_specs.append(param_spec)
188|
189|    return functools.partial(_apply_param_specs, param_specs)
190|
191|
192|def update_param_specs(
193|    param_specs: Iterable[Param] | None, new_specs: Iterable[Param]
194|) -> list[Param]:
195|    """Produces all combinations of the given sets of specs."""
196|    if param_specs is None:
197|        return list(new_specs)
198|
199|    # New specs must be combined with old specs by *multiplying* them.
200|    combined_specs = []
201|    for new_spec in new_specs:
202|        for spec in param_specs:
203|            spec_copy = spec.copy()
204|            spec_copy.update(new_spec)
205|            combined_specs.append(spec_copy)
206|    return combined_specs

196|def _highest_under_upper_bound(
197|    operator: str, version_str: str
198|) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
199|    """Return the highest ``(major, minor)`` fully below a ``<``/``<=`` clause.
200|
201|    Installers resolve ``X.Y`` to its latest patch release, so the pick must
202|    allow *every* ``X.Y`` patch; that is always the minor below the bound's:
203|    ``<3.12`` -> ``3.11``, ``<=3.12`` -> ``3.11``, ``<3.12.4`` -> ``3.11``
204|    (``3.12`` would install a patch that may exceed ``3.12.4``). Returns
205|    ``None`` for other operators or when no minor version can be picked
206|    (``<4``, ``<3.0``).
207|    """
208|    if operator not in {"<", "<="}:
209|        return None
210|    try:
211|        release = version.Version(version_str).release
212|    except version.InvalidVersion:
213|        return None
214|    if len(release) < 2:
215|        return None
216|    major, minor = release[0], release[1] - 1
217|    if minor < 0:
218|        return None
219|    return major, minor

222|def _concrete_install_target(interpreter: str) -> str | None:
223|    """Return a concrete version to hand to an installer, or ``None``.
224|
225|    Non-range specs (names, concrete versions, paths) are returned unchanged.
226|    For a PEP 440 range (``>=3.14``) the floor of the first lower-bound clause
227|    is returned (``3.14``) so a concrete interpreter can be downloaded. Without
228|    a lower bound, the highest version under the tightest upper bound that the
229|    other clauses allow is used instead (``<3.12`` -> ``3.11``,
230|    ``<3.14,!=3.13.*`` -> ``3.12``). A non-CPython implementation prefix is
231|    preserved (``pypy>=3.10`` -> ``pypy3.10``) so the right flavor is installed;
232|    the version already carries any free-threaded ``t`` suffix. Ranges with no
233|    usable bound (``!=3.12``, ``<4``) return ``None``.
234|    """
235|    from python_discovery import PythonSpec  # noqa: PLC0415
236|
237|    spec = PythonSpec.from_string_spec(interpreter)
238|    if spec.version_specifier is None:
239|        return interpreter
240|    impl = spec.implementation
241|    prefix = impl if impl and impl != "cpython" else ""
242|    for specifier in spec.version_specifier.specifiers:
243|        if specifier.operator in {">=", "==", "~=", ">"}:
244|            return f"{prefix}{specifier.version_str}"
245|
246|    # python-discovery's specifiers don't understand the free-threaded "t"
247|    # suffix, so strip it up front and do the version arithmetic with packaging.
248|    suffix = (
249|        "t"
250|        if any(s.version_str.endswith("t") for s in spec.version_specifier.specifiers)
251|        else ""
252|    )
253|    clauses = [
254|        (s.operator, s.version_str.removesuffix("t"))
255|        for s in spec.version_specifier.specifiers
256|    ]
257|    candidates = [
258|        candidate
259|        for op, ver in clauses
260|        if (candidate := _highest_under_upper_bound(op, ver)) is not None
261|    ]
262|    if not candidates:
263|        return None
264|    try:
265|        allowed = specifiers.SpecifierSet(",".join(f"{op}{ver}" for op, ver in clauses))
266|    except specifiers.InvalidSpecifier:
267|        return None
268|    # The tightest upper bound wins, but another clause (an "!=") can exclude
269|    # the pick, so step down through the minors until one clears the whole set.
270|    major, top_minor = min(candidates)
271|    for minor in range(top_minor, -1, -1):
272|        if allowed.contains(f"{major}.{minor}"):
273|            return f"{prefix}{major}.{minor}{suffix}"
274|    return None

341|    """Attempts to install a given python version with pbs-installer.
342|
343|    Returns the full path to the installed executable, or None if installation failed.
344|    """
345|

348|        r"^(?P<impl>pypy|cpython|python)?[-_\.]?(?P<xyz_ver>\d(\.\d+)?(\.\d+))?$",
349|        python_version,

361|    )
362|    xyz_ver: str = match["xyz_ver"]

376|    try:

519|    ) -> dict[str, str | None]:
520|        """

522|        the outer environment be excluded. The initial env can be empty.
523|        """
524|

711|def _parse_conda_args(args: Sequence[str]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
712|    """Split conda-style args into channels and specs, expanding ``--file``.
713|
714|    Only ``-c``/``--channel`` and ``--file`` are accepted; any other option
715|    raises ``ValueError``.
716|    """
717|    channels: list[str] = []
718|    specs: list[str] = []

720|    for param in params:

722|        if opt in {"-c", "--channel", "--file"} and not value:
723|            value = next(params)
724|        if opt in {"-c", "--channel"}:
725|            channels.append(value)
726|        elif opt == "--file":
727|            specs.extend(_rattler.read_spec_file(value))
728|        elif param.startswith("-"):
729|            msg = f"The rattler backend does not support the {param!r} option."
730|            raise ValueError(msg)
731|        else:
732|            specs.append(param)
733|    return channels, specs

1100|) -> ProcessEnv:

1108|

1112|            raise ValueError(msg)

160|def _analyze_type(tp: Any) -> tuple[str, tuple[Any, ...] | None]:
161|    """Classify a field type for argparse.

164|    choices, if any.

166|    origin = typing.get_origin(tp)
167|    if origin in {typing.Union, types.UnionType}:
168|        non_none = [a for a in typing.get_args(tp) if a is not type(None)]
169|        kinds = {_analyze_type(a)[0] for a in non_none}
170|        if len(kinds) == 1:
171|            return _analyze_type(non_none[0])
172|        return ("value", None)
173|    if origin is Literal:
174|        return ("value", typing.get_args(tp))
175|    if tp is bool:
176|        return ("flag", None)
177|    if origin in {list, tuple} or tp in {list, tuple}:
178|        return ("list", None)

182|def to_argv(config: OptionsBase) -> list[str]:
183|    """Serialize a config back into the CLI arguments that reproduce it.
184|
185|    The output, parsed and finalized again, restores every forwardable value.
186|    Options marked ``Forward.NEVER`` are skipped; new options are forwarded by
187|    default. An ``IF_CHANGED`` option is emitted when its value was explicitly
188|    set (per provenance) or differs from the field default — provenance alone
189|    is not enough, or an explicit CLI value that equals the default (say,
190|    ``--reuse-venv=no``) would be dropped and a Noxfile could override it in
191|    the reparsing process. Positional arguments (posargs) are emitted last,
192|    after ``--``.
193|    """
194|    argv: list[str] = []
195|    tail: list[str] = []
196|    defaults = type(config)()
197|    for field in attrs.fields(type(config)):
198|        option = _get_opt(field)
199|        if option is None or option.forward is Forward.NEVER:
200|            continue
201|        value = getattr(config, field.name)
202|        if option.positional:
203|            if value:
204|                tail = ["--", *(str(v) for v in value)]
205|            continue
206|        if (
207|            option.forward is Forward.IF_CHANGED
208|            and config.provenance(field.name) is Source.DEFAULT
209|            and value == getattr(defaults, field.name)
210|        ):
211|            continue
212|        choices = option.argparse_kwargs.get("choices")
213|        if choices is not None and value not in choices:
214|            # Values the CLI grammar can't express (e.g. the noxfile-only
215|            # "uv|virtualenv" fallback syntax); the child re-derives them.
216|            continue
217|        if option.negative_flags:
218|            argv.append(option.flags[-1] if value else option.negative_flags[-1])
219|            continue
220|        flag = option.flags[-1]
221|        if isinstance(value, bool):
222|            if value:
223|                argv.append(flag)
224|        elif isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
225|            if value:
226|                argv += [flag, *(str(v) for v in value)]
227|        elif value is not None:
228|            argv += [flag, str(value)]
229|    return argv + tail

232|def apply_noxfile_values(
233|    config: OptionsBase, noxfile_config: OptionsBase, *, skip: Iterable[str] = ()
234|) -> None:
235|    """Copy fields set in the noxfile into the config where nothing outranks them."""
236|    skip = set(skip)
237|    for field in attrs.fields(type(noxfile_config)):
238|        name = field.name
239|        if _get_opt(field) is None or name in skip:
240|            continue
241|        if noxfile_config.provenance(name) is Source.DEFAULT:
242|            continue
243|        if config.provenance(name) is Source.DEFAULT:
244|            config.set_value(name, getattr(noxfile_config, name), Source.NOXFILE)

247|class Options(Generic[ConfigT]):
248|    """The full option set: builds the parser and config objects from the model.
249|
250|    Args:
251|        config_class: The attrs class holding every option (the CLI surface).
252|        groups: Mapping of group key to (title, description) for ``--help``.
253|        description: The parser description.
254|        finalize: Called with the fresh config after parsing, before returning;
255|            resolves aliases and cross-field options. ``ArgumentError`` raised
256|            here is reported via ``parser.error``.
257|    """
258|
259|    def __init__(
260|        self,
261|        config_class: type[ConfigT],
262|        *,
263|        groups: dict[str, tuple[str, str]],
264|        description: str,
265|        finalize: Callable[[Any], None] | None = None,
266|    ) -> None:
267|        self.config_class = config_class
268|        self.groups = groups
269|        self.description = description
270|        self.finalize = finalize
271|        attrs.resolve_types(config_class)
272|
273|    def _argparse_kwargs(
274|        self, field: attrs.Attribute[Any], option: Opt
275|    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
276|        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
277|        kind, choices = _analyze_type(field.type)
278|        if kind == "flag":
279|            kwargs["action"] = "store_true"
280|        elif kind == "list":
281|            kwargs["nargs"] = "*"
282|        if choices:
283|            kwargs["choices"] = list(choices)
284|        kwargs.update(option.argparse_kwargs)
285|        return kwargs
286|
287|    def parser(self) -> ArgumentParser:
288|        """Build the ``ArgumentParser`` for the model.
289|
290|        Parsing is sparse: only flags actually passed appear in the resulting
291|        namespace (via ``argparse.SUPPRESS``), so provenance is exact.
292|        """
293|        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
294|            description=self.description, add_help=False, allow_abbrev=False
295|        )
296|        groups = {
297|            name: parser.add_argument_group(title, description)
298|            for name, (title, description) in self.groups.items()
299|        }
300|        for field in attrs.fields(self.config_class):
301|            option = _get_opt(field)
302|            if option is None or option.hidden:
303|                continue
304|            if option.group is None:
305|                msg = f"Option {field.name} must either have a group or be hidden."
306|                raise ValueError(msg)
307|            group = groups[option.group]
308|            if option.positional:
309|                group.add_argument(
310|                    field.name,
311|                    help=option.help,
312|                    default=[],
313|                    **option.argparse_kwargs,
314|                )
315|                continue
316|            argument = group.add_argument(
317|                *option.flags,
318|                dest=field.name,
319|                help=option.help,
320|                default=argparse.SUPPRESS,
321|                **self._argparse_kwargs(field, option),
322|            )
323|            if option.completer:
324|                argument.completer = option.completer  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
325|            if option.negative_flags:
326|                group.add_argument(
327|                    *option.negative_flags,
328|                    dest=field.name,
329|                    action="store_false",
330|                    default=argparse.SUPPRESS,
331|                    help=f"Disables {option.flags[-1]} if it is enabled in the Noxfile.",
332|                )
333|        return parser
334|
335|    def print_help(self) -> None:
336|        self.parser().print_help()
337|
338|    def expand(self, namespace: Namespace | ConfigT) -> ConfigT:
339|        """Build a full config from a sparse argparse namespace.
340|
341|        Values present in the namespace were passed on the command line;
342|        everything else falls back to the environment variable (if declared)
343|        and then the field default. A config passed in (e.g. from
344|        :meth:`namespace` in tests) is returned unchanged.
345|        """
346|        if isinstance(namespace, self.config_class):
347|            return namespace
348|        sparse = vars(namespace)
349|        config = self.config_class()
350|        for field in attrs.fields(self.config_class):
351|            option = _get_opt(field)
352|            if option is None:
353|                continue
354|            if field.name in sparse:
355|                value = sparse[field.name]
356|                # argparse always fills positionals in; empty means not given.
357|                if option.positional and not value:
358|                    continue
359|                config.set_value(field.name, value, Source.COMMAND_LINE)
360|            elif option.env_var and (env_value := os.environ.get(option.env_var)):
361|                kind, _ = _analyze_type(field.type)
362|                value = env_value.split(",") if kind == "list" else env_value
363|                config.set_value(field.name, value, Source.ENVIRONMENT)
364|        return config
365|
366|    def parse_args(self, args: list[str] | None = None) -> ConfigT:
367|        parser = self.parser()
368|        argcomplete.autocomplete(parser)
369|        namespace = parser.parse_args(args)
370|        try:
371|            config = self.expand(namespace)
372|        except ValueError as err:
373|            # Bad environment-variable values fail their field validator.
374|            parser.error(str(err.args[0]) if err.args else str(err))
375|        try:
376|            if self.finalize is not None:
377|                self.finalize(config)
378|        except ArgumentError as err:
379|            parser.error(str(err))
380|        return config
381|
382|    def namespace(self, **kwargs: Any) -> ConfigT:
383|        """Return a config with every option at its default.
384|
385|        kwargs set values in a checked way - you can not set an option that
386|        does not exist. This is useful for testing.
387|        """
388|        fields = attrs.fields_dict(self.config_class)
389|        config = self.config_class()
390|        for key, value in kwargs.items():
391|            if key not in fields or _get_opt(fields[key]) is None:
392|                msg = f"{key} is not an option."
393|                raise KeyError(msg)
394|            config.set_value(key, value, Source.COMMAND_LINE)
395|        return config

70|def _load_and_exec_nox_module(global_config: NoxConfig) -> types.ModuleType:
71|    """
72|    Loads, executes, then returns the global_config Nox module.
73|
74|    Args:
75|        global_config (Namespace): The global config.
76|
77|    Raises:
78|        IOError: If the Nox module cannot be loaded. This
79|            exception is chosen such that it will be caught
80|            by load_nox_module and logged appropriately.
81|
82|    Returns:
83|        types.ModuleType: The initialised Nox module.
84|    """
85|    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
86|        "user_nox_module", str(global_config.noxfile)
87|    )
88|    assert spec is not None  # If None, fatal importlib error, would crash anyway
89|
90|    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
91|    assert module is not None  # If None, fatal importlib error, would crash anyway
92|
93|    sys.modules["user_nox_module"] = module
94|
95|    loader = spec.loader
96|    assert loader is not None  # If None, fatal importlib error, would crash anyway
97|    # See https://docs.python.org/3/library/importlib.html#importing-a-source-file-directly
98|    loader.exec_module(module)
99|    return module

102|def load_nox_module(global_config: NoxConfig) -> types.ModuleType | int:
103|    """Load the user's Noxfile and return the module object for it.
104|
105|    .. note::
106|
107|        This task has two side effects; it makes ``global_config.noxfile``
108|        an absolute path, and changes the working directory of the process.
109|
110|    Args:
111|        global_config (.nox.main.GlobalConfig): The global config.
112|
113|    Returns:
114|        module: The module designated by the Noxfile path.
115|    """
116|    # Be sure to expand variables
117|    global_config_noxfile = os.path.expandvars(global_config.noxfile)
118|
119|    # Make sure we only expand the parent dir just in case the noxfile is a symlink
120|    noxfile_parent_dir = os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(global_config_noxfile))
121|
122|    # Save the absolute path to the Noxfile.
123|    # This will inoculate it if Nox changes paths because of an implicit
124|    # or explicit chdir (like the one below).
125|    global_config.noxfile = os.path.join(
126|        noxfile_parent_dir, os.path.basename(global_config_noxfile)
127|    )
128|
129|    try:
130|        # Check ``nox.needs_version`` by parsing the AST.
131|        check_nox_version(global_config.noxfile)
132|
133|        # Move to the path where the Noxfile is.
134|        # This will ensure that the Noxfile's path is on sys.path, and that
135|        # import-time path resolutions work the way the Noxfile author would
136|        # guess. The original working directory (the directory that Nox was
137|        # invoked from) gets stored by the .invoke_from "option" in _options.
138|        os.chdir(noxfile_parent_dir)
139|
140|    except (VersionCheckFailed, InvalidVersionSpecifier) as error:
141|        logger.error(str(error))
142|        return 2
143|    except FileNotFoundError:
144|        logger.error(
145|            f"Failed to load Noxfile {global_config.noxfile}, no such file exists."
146|        )
147|        return 2
148|    except OSError:
149|        logger.exception(f"Failed to load Noxfile {global_config.noxfile}")
150|        return 2
151|
152|    return _load_and_exec_nox_module(global_config)

169|def discover_manifest(
170|    module: types.ModuleType | int, global_config: NoxConfig
171|) -> Manifest:
172|    """Discover all session functions in the Noxfile module.
173|
174|    Args:
175|        module (module): The Noxfile module.
176|        global_config (~nox.main.GlobalConfig): The global configuration.
177|
178|    Returns:
179|        ~.Manifest: A manifest of session functions.
180|    """
181|    # Find any function added to the session registry (meaning it was
182|    # decorated with @nox.session); do not sort these, as they are being
183|    # sorted by decorator call time.
184|    functions = registry.get()
185|
186|    # Get the docstring from the Noxfile
187|    module_docstring = module.__doc__
188|
189|    # Return the final dictionary of session functions.
190|    return Manifest(functions, global_config, module_docstring)

193|def filter_manifest(manifest: Manifest, global_config: NoxConfig) -> Manifest | int:
194|    """Filter the manifest according to the provided configuration.
195|
196|    Args:
197|        manifest (~.Manifest): The manifest of sessions to be run.
198|        global_config (~nox.main.GlobalConfig): The global configuration.
199|
200|    Returns:
201|        Union[~.Manifest,int]: ``3`` if a specified session is not found,
202|            the manifest otherwise (to be sent to the next task).
203|
204|    """
205|    # Shouldn't happen unless the Noxfile is empty
206|    if not manifest:
207|        logger.error(f"No sessions found in {global_config.noxfile}.")
208|        return 3
209|
210|    # Filter by the name of any explicit sessions.
211|    # This can raise KeyError if a specified session does not exist;
212|    # log this if it happens. The sessions does not come from the Noxfile
213|    # if keywords is not empty or tags are supplied.
214|    if global_config.tags is None and not global_config.keywords:
215|        if global_config.sessions is None:
216|            manifest.filter_by_default()
217|        else:
218|            try:
219|                manifest.filter_by_name(global_config.sessions)
220|            except KeyError as exc:
221|                logger.error("Error while collecting sessions.")
222|                logger.error(exc.args[0])
223|                return 3
224|
225|    if not manifest and not global_config.list_sessions:
226|        print("No sessions selected. Please select a session with -s <session name>.\n")
227|        _produce_listing(manifest, global_config)
228|        return 0
229|
230|    # Filter by python interpreter versions.
231|    if global_config.pythons:
232|        manifest.filter_by_python_interpreter(global_config.pythons)
233|        if not manifest and not global_config.list_sessions:
234|            logger.error("Python version selection caused no sessions to be selected.")
235|            return 3
236|
237|    # Filter by tags.
238|    if global_config.tags is not None:
239|        manifest.filter_by_tags(global_config.tags)
240|        if not manifest and not global_config.list_sessions:
241|            logger.error("Tag selection caused no sessions to be selected.")
242|            return 3
243|
244|    # Filter by keywords.
245|    if global_config.keywords:
246|        try:
247|            ast.parse(global_config.keywords, mode="eval")
248|        except SyntaxError:
249|            logger.error(
250|                "Error while collecting sessions: keywords argument must be a Python"
251|                " expression."
252|            )
253|            return 3
254|
255|        # This function never errors, but may cause an empty list of sessions
256|        # (which is an error condition later).
257|        manifest.filter_by_keywords(global_config.keywords)
258|
259|    if not manifest and not global_config.list_sessions:
260|        logger.error("No sessions selected after filtering by keyword.")
261|        return 3
262|
263|    # Add dependencies, unless --no-dependencies limits the run to only the
264|    # explicitly selected sessions (as the parallel runner's children do).
265|    # Even then, a ``requires=`` entry naming a session that doesn't exist is
266|    # still an error, the prerequisites just aren't queued.
267|    try:
268|        if global_config.no_dependencies:
269|            for session, selected in manifest.list_all_sessions():
270|                if selected:
271|                    list(session.get_direct_dependencies())
272|        else:
273|            manifest.add_dependencies()
274|    except (KeyError, CycleError) as exc:
275|        logger.error("Error while resolving session dependencies.")
276|        logger.error(exc.args[0])
277|        return 3
278|
279|    # Return the modified manifest.
280|    return manifest

283|def _produce_listing(manifest: Manifest, global_config: NoxConfig) -> None:
284|    # If the user just asked for a list of sessions, print that
285|    # and any docstring specified in noxfile.py and be done. This
286|    # can also be called if Noxfile sessions is an empty list.
287|
288|    if manifest.module_docstring:
289|        print(manifest.module_docstring.strip(), end="\n\n")
290|
291|    print(f"Sessions defined in {global_config.noxfile}:\n")
292|
293|    reset = parse_colors("reset") if global_config.color else ""
294|    selected_color = parse_colors("cyan") if global_config.color else ""
295|    skipped_color = parse_colors("white") if global_config.color else ""
296|
297|    for session, selected in manifest.list_all_sessions():
298|        marker = "*" if selected else "-"
299|        color = selected_color if selected else skipped_color
300|        tag_color = (
301|            (parse_colors("purple") if selected else parse_colors("light_purple"))
302|            if global_config.color
303|            else ""
304|        )
305|
306|        tags = f" {tag_color}[{','.join(session.tags)}]{reset}" if session.tags else ""
307|        description = f" -> {session.description}" if session.description else ""
308|
309|        print(f"{marker} {color}{session.friendly_name}{reset}{tags}{description}")
310|
311|    print(
312|        f"\nsessions marked with {selected_color}*{reset} are selected, sessions marked"
313|        f" with {skipped_color}-{reset} are skipped."
314|    )

334|def honor_list_request(manifest: Manifest, global_config: NoxConfig) -> Manifest | int:
335|    """If --list was passed, simply list the manifest and exit cleanly.
336|
337|    Args:
338|        manifest (~.Manifest): The manifest of sessions to be run.
339|        global_config (~nox.main.GlobalConfig): The global configuration.
340|
341|    Returns:
342|        Union[~.Manifest,int]: ``0`` if a listing is all that is requested,
343|            the manifest otherwise (to be sent to the next task).
344|    """
345|    if not (global_config.list_sessions or global_config.json):
346|        return manifest
347|
348|    # JSON output requires list sessions also be specified
349|    if global_config.json and not global_config.list_sessions:
350|        logger.error("Must specify --list-sessions with --json")
351|        return 3
352|
353|    if global_config.json:
354|        _produce_json_listing(manifest, global_config)
355|    else:
356|        _produce_listing(manifest, global_config)
357|
358|    return 0
