361|def honor_usage_request(manifest: Manifest, global_config: NoxConfig) -> Manifest | int:
362|    """If --usage was passed, print the full docstring of the session and exit.
363|    Raise an error if the session does not exist or has no docstring to print.
364|
365|    Args:
366|        manifest (~.Manifest): The manifest of sessions to be run.
367|        global_config (~nox.main.GlobalConfig): The global configuration.
368|
369|    Returns:
370|        Union[~.Manifest,int]: ``0`` if usage is printed,
371|            the manifest otherwise (to be sent to the next task).
372|    """
373|    if not global_config.usage:
374|        return manifest
375|
376|    name = global_config.usage[0]
377|
378|    # Search all sessions, not just the filtered queue, so that
379|    # non-default sessions can also be looked up.
380|    session = None
381|    for _ in manifest._all_sessions:
382|        if _.name == name or name in _.signatures:
383|            session = _
384|            break
385|
386|    if session is None:
387|        logger.error("Session %s not found.", name)
388|        return 1
389|
390|    full_description = session.full_description
391|    if full_description is None:
392|        logger.error("Session %s has no docstring.", name)
393|        return 1
394|
395|    print(full_description)
396|    return 0

399|def run_manifest(manifest: Manifest, global_config: NoxConfig) -> list[Result]:
400|    """Run the full manifest of sessions.
401|
402|    Args:
403|        manifest (~.Manifest): The manifest of sessions to be run.
404|        global_config (~nox.main.GlobalConfig): The global configuration.
405|
406|    Returns:
407|        tuple[~nox.sessions.Session,~.SessionStatus]: A two-tuple of the
408|            sessions and the result of each session that was run.
409|    """
410|    # When --parallel/-j requests more than one job, hand off to the parallel
411|    # scheduler, which runs independent sessions in their own subprocesses.
412|    jobs = global_config.parallel or 1
413|    if jobs > 1 and not any(
414|        resolve_allow_parallel(global_config, session.func)
415|        for session, selected in manifest.list_all_sessions()
416|        if selected
417|    ):
418|        logger.warning(
419|            "No selected session allows parallel execution; ignoring --parallel"
420|            " and running sequentially. Opt in with allow_parallel=True or"
421|            " --allow-parallel."
422|        )
423|        jobs = 1
424|    if jobs > 1:
425|        # Imported lazily so sequential runs don't pay for the parallel machinery.
426|        from nox._parallel import run_manifest_parallel  # noqa: PLC0415
427|
428|        return run_manifest_parallel(manifest, global_config, jobs)
429|
430|    results = []
431|
432|    # Iterate over each session in the manifest, and execute it.
433|    #
434|    # Note that it is possible for the manifest to be altered in any given
435|    # iteration.
436|    for session in manifest:
437|        # possibly raise warnings associated with this session
438|        if WARN_PYTHONS_IGNORED in session.func.should_warn:
439|            logger.warning(
440|                f"Session {session.name} is set to run with venv_backend='none', "
441|                "IGNORING its"
442|                f" python={session.func.should_warn[WARN_PYTHONS_IGNORED]} parametrization. "
443|            )
444|
445|        result = session.execute()
446|        name = session.friendly_name
447|        status = result.imperfect
448|        result.log(f"Session {name} {status}.")
449|        results.append(result)
450|
451|        # Sanity check: If we are supposed to stop on the first error case,
452|        # then abort now.
453|        if not result and global_config.stop_on_first_error:
454|            return results
455|
456|    # The entire manifest has been processed; return the results.
457|    return results

460|Sequence_Results_T = TypeVar("Sequence_Results_T", bound=Sequence[Result])

462|
463|def print_summary(
464|    results: Sequence_Results_T,
465|    global_config: NoxConfig,
466|) -> Sequence_Results_T:
467|    """Print a summary of the results.
468|
469|    Args:
470|        results (Sequence[~nox.sessions.Result]): A list of Result objects.
471|        global_config (~nox.main.GlobalConfig): The global configuration.
472|
473|    Returns:
474|        results (Sequence[~nox.sessions.Result]): The results passed
475|            to this function, unmodified.
476|    """
477|    # Sanity check: Do not print results if there was only one session run.
478|    if len(results) <= 1:
479|        return results
480|
481|    # Iterate over the results and print the result for each in a
482|    # human-readable way. In parallel mode the runner records the wall-clock
483|    # time; otherwise sum the per-session durations (which run back-to-back).
484|    total_duration = global_config.parallel_wall_time
485|    if total_duration is None:
486|        total_duration = sum(result.duration for result in results)
487|    duration_str = _duration_str(total_duration, " in {time}")
488|    logger.session_info(f"Ran {len(results)} sessions{duration_str}:")
489|    for result in results:
490|        name = result.session.friendly_name
491|        status = result.status.name.lower()
492|        duration_str = _duration_str(result.duration, ", took {time}")
493|        if result.status is Status.SKIPPED and result.reason:
494|            result.log(f"* {name}: {status} ({result.reason}){duration_str}")
495|        else:
496|            result.log(f"* {name}: {status}{duration_str}")
497|
498|    # Return the results that were sent to this function.
499|    return results

501|
502|def create_report(
503|    results: Sequence_Results_T, global_config: NoxConfig
504|) -> Sequence_Results_T:
505|    """Write a report to the location designated in the config, if any.
506|
507|    Args:
508|        results (Sequence[~nox.sessions.Result]): A list of Result objects
509|        global_config (~nox.main.GlobalConfig): The global configuration.
510|
511|    Returns:
512|        results (Sequence[~nox.sessions.Result]): The results passed
513|            to this function, unmodified.
514|    """
515|    # Sanity check: If no JSON report was requested, this is a no-op.
516|    if global_config.report is None:
517|        return results
518|
519|    # Write the JSON report.
520|    with open(global_config.report, "w", encoding="utf-8") as report_file:
521|        json.dump(
522|            {
523|                "result": int(all(results)),
524|                "sessions": [result.serialize() for result in results],
525|            },
526|            report_file,
527|            indent=2,
528|        )
529|
530|    # Return back the results passed to this task.
531|    return results
532|
533|
534|def final_reduce(results: list[Result], global_config: NoxConfig) -> int:  # noqa: ARG001
535|    """Reduce the results to a final exit code.
536|
537|    Args:
538|        results (Sequence[~nox.sessions.Result]): A list of Result objects
539|        global_config (~nox.main.GlobalConfig): The global configuration.
540|
541|    Returns:
542|        int: The final status code; ``0`` for success and ``1`` for failure.
543|    """
544|    if not all(results):
545|        return 1
546|    return 0

50|class Manifest:
51|    """Session manifest.
52|
53|    The session manifest provides the source of truth for the sequence of
54|    sessions that should be run by Nox.
55|
56|    It is possible for this to be mutated during execution. This allows for
57|    useful use cases, such as for one session to "notify" another or
58|    "chain" to another.
59|
60|    Args:
61|        session_functions (Mapping[str, function]): The registry of discovered
62|            session functions.
63|        global_config (.nox.main.GlobalConfig): The global configuration.
64|        module_docstring (Optional[str]): The user noxfile.py docstring.
65|            Defaults to `None`.
66|    """
67|
68|    def __init__(
69|        self,
70|        session_functions: Mapping[str, Func],
71|        global_config: NoxConfig,
72|        module_docstring: str | None = None,
73|    ) -> None:
74|        self._all_sessions: list[SessionRunner] = []
75|        self._queue: list[SessionRunner] = []
76|        self._consumed: list[SessionRunner] = []
77|        self._config: NoxConfig = global_config
78|        self.module_docstring: str | None = module_docstring
79|
80|        # Create the sessions based on the provided session functions.
81|        for name, func in session_functions.items():
82|            for session in self.make_session(name, func):
83|                self.add_session(session)
84|
85|    def __contains__(self, needle: str | SessionRunner) -> bool:
86|        return (
87|            needle in self._queue
88|            or needle in self._consumed
89|            or any(
90|                session.name == needle or needle in session.signatures
91|                for session in itertools.chain(self._queue, self._consumed)
92|            )
93|        )
94|
95|    def __iter__(self) -> Manifest:
96|        return self
97|
98|    def __getitem__(self, key: str) -> SessionRunner:
99|        for session in itertools.chain(self._queue, self._consumed):
100|            if session.name == key or key in session.signatures:
101|                return session
102|        raise KeyError(key)
103|
104|    def __next__(self) -> SessionRunner:
105|        """Return the next item in the queue.
106|
107|        Raises:
108|            StopIteration: If the queue has been entirely consumed.
109|        """
110|        if not self._queue:
111|            raise StopIteration
112|        session = self._queue.pop(0)
113|        self._consumed.append(session)
114|        return session
115|
116|    def __len__(self) -> int:
117|        return len(self._queue) + len(self._consumed)

119|    def list_all_sessions(self) -> Iterator[tuple[SessionRunner, bool]]:

162|    def filter_by_name(self, specified_sessions: Iterable[str]) -> None:
163|        """Filter sessions in the queue based on the user-specified names.

170|            KeyError: If any explicitly listed sessions are not found.

173|        # whether they are individually specified.
174|        self._queue = [
175|            session
176|            for session_name in specified_sessions
177|            for session in self._queue
178|            if _normalized_session_match(session_name, session)

182|        all_sessions = set(
183|            map(
184|                _normalize_arg,
185|                (
186|                    itertools.chain(
187|                        [x.name for x in self._all_sessions if x.name],
188|                        *[x.signatures for x in self._all_sessions],
189|                    )
190|                ),
191|            )

194|            session_name
195|            for session_name in specified_sessions

239|    def add_dependencies(self) -> None:
240|        """Add direct and recursive dependencies to the queue.
241|
242|        Raises:
243|            KeyError: If any depended-on sessions are not found.
244|            ~nox._resolver.CycleError: If a dependency cycle is encountered.
245|        """
246|        sessions_by_id = self.all_sessions_by_signature
247|
248|        # For each session that was parametrized from a list of Pythons, create a fake
249|        # parent session that depends on it.
250|        parent_sessions: set[SessionRunner] = set()
251|        for (
252|            parent_name,
253|            parametrized_sessions,
254|        ) in self.parametrized_sessions_by_name.items():
255|            parent_func = _null_session_func.copy()
256|            parent_func.requires = [
257|                session.signatures[0]
258|                for session in parametrized_sessions
259|                if session.signatures
260|            ]
261|            parent_session = SessionRunner(
262|                parent_name, [], parent_func, self._config, self, multi=False
263|            )
264|            parent_sessions.add(parent_session)
265|            sessions_by_id[parent_name] = parent_session
266|
267|        # Construct the dependency graph. Note that this is done lazily with iterators
268|        # so that we won't raise if a session that doesn't actually need to run declares
269|        # missing/improper dependencies.
270|        dependency_graph = {
271|            session: session.get_direct_dependencies(sessions_by_id)
272|            for session in sessions_by_id.values()
273|        }
274|
275|        # Sessions without any signatures (e.g. the placeholder session created
276|        # when a parametrized session has an empty list of parameters) are not
277|        # in ``sessions_by_id``, so add any missing queued sessions to the graph.
278|        for session in self._queue:
279|            dependency_graph.setdefault(
280|                session, session.get_direct_dependencies(sessions_by_id)
281|            )
282|
283|        # Resolve the dependency graph.
284|        root = cast("SessionRunner", object())  # sentinel
285|        try:
286|            resolved_graph = list(
287|                lazy_stable_topo_sort({**dependency_graph, root: self._queue}, root)
288|            )
289|        except CycleError as exc:
290|            raise CycleError(
291|                "Sessions are in a dependency cycle: "
292|                + " -> ".join(session.name for session in exc.args[1])
293|            ) from exc
294|
295|        # Remove fake parent sessions from the resolved graph.
296|        self._queue = [
297|            session for session in resolved_graph if session not in parent_sessions
298|        ]

300|    def make_session(
301|        self, name: str, func: Func, *, multi: bool = False
302|    ) -> list[SessionRunner]:
303|        """Create a session object from the session function.
304|
305|        Args:
306|            name (str): The name of the session.
307|            func (function): The session function.
308|            multi (bool): Whether the function is a member of a set of sessions
309|                with different interpreters.
310|
311|        Returns:
312|            Sequence[~nox.session.Session]: A sequence of Session objects
313|                bound to this manifest and configuration.
314|        """
315|        sessions = []
316|
317|        # If the backend is "none", we won't parametrize `python`.
318|        backend = (
319|            self._config.force_venv_backend
320|            or func.venv_backend
321|            or self._config.default_venv_backend
322|        )
323|        if backend == "none" and isinstance(func.python, (list, tuple, set)):
324|            # we can not log a warning here since the session is maybe deselected.
325|            # instead let's set a flag, to warn later when session is actually run.
326|            func.should_warn[WARN_PYTHONS_IGNORED] = func.python
327|            func.python = False
328|
329|        if self._config.extra_pythons:
330|            # If extra python is provided, expand the func.python list to
331|            # include additional python interpreters
332|            extra_pythons: Sequence[str] = self._config.extra_pythons
333|            if isinstance(func.python, (list, tuple, set)):
334|                func.python = _unique_list(*func.python, *extra_pythons)
335|            elif not multi and func.python:
336|                # If this is multi, but there is only a single interpreter, it
337|                # is the reentrant case. The extra_python interpreter shouldn't
338|                # be added in that case. If func.python is False, the session
339|                # has no backend; if None, it uses the same interpreter as Nox.
340|                # Otherwise, add the extra specified python.
341|                assert isinstance(func.python, str)
342|                func.python = _unique_list(func.python, *extra_pythons)
343|            elif not func.python and self._config.force_pythons:
344|                # If a python is forced by the user, but the underlying function
345|                # has no version parametrised, add it as sole occupant to func.python
346|                func.python = _unique_list(*extra_pythons)
347|
348|        # If the func has the python attribute set to a list, we'll need
349|        # to expand them. Duplicates would make identical sessions.
350|        if isinstance(func.python, (list, tuple, set)):
351|            for python in _unique_list(*func.python):
352|                single_func = func.copy()
353|                single_func.python = python
354|                sessions.extend(self.make_session(name, single_func, multi=True))
355|
356|            return sessions
357|
358|        # Simple case: If this function is not parametrized, then make
359|        # a simple session.
360|        if not hasattr(func, "parametrize"):
361|            long_names = []
362|            if not multi:
363|                long_names.append(name)
364|            if func.python:
365|                long_names.append(f"{name}-{func.python}")
366|
367|            return [
368|                SessionRunner(name, long_names, func, self._config, self, multi=multi)
369|            ]
370|
371|        # Since this function is parametrized, we need to add a distinct
372|        # session for each permutation.
373|        parametrize = func.parametrize
374|        calls = Call.generate_calls(func, parametrize)
375|        for call in calls:
376|            long_names = []
377|            if not multi or (
378|                self._config.force_pythons
379|                and call.python in (self._config.extra_pythons or ())
380|            ):
381|                long_names.append(f"{name}{call.session_signature}")
382|
383|            if func.python:
384|                long_names.append(f"{name}-{func.python}{call.session_signature}")
385|                # Ensure that specifying session-python will run all parameterizations.
386|                long_names.append(f"{name}-{func.python}")
387|
388|            sessions.append(
389|                SessionRunner(name, long_names, call, self._config, self, multi=multi)
390|            )
391|
392|        # Edge case: If the parameters made it such that there were no valid
393|        # calls, add an empty, do-nothing session.
394|        if not calls:
395|            sessions.append(
396|                SessionRunner(
397|                    name, [], _null_session_func, self._config, self, multi=multi
398|                )
399|            )
400|
401|        # Return the list of sessions.
402|        return sessions

404|    def notify(
405|        self, session: str | SessionRunner, posargs: Iterable[str] | None = None
406|    ) -> bool:
407|        """Enqueue the specified session in the queue.
408|
409|        If the session is already in the queue, or has been run already,
410|        then this is a no-op.
411|
412|        Args:
413|            session (Union[str, ~nox.session.Session]): The session to be
414|                enqueued.
415|            posargs (Optional[List[str]]): If given, sets the positional
416|                arguments *only* for the queued session. Otherwise, the
417|                standard globally available positional arguments will be
418|                used instead.
419|
420|        Returns:
421|            bool: Whether the session was added to the queue.
422|
423|        Raises:
424|            ValueError: If the session was not found.
425|        """
426|        # Sanity check: If this session is already in the queue, this is
427|        # a no-op.
428|        if session in self:
429|            return False
430|
431|        # Locate the session in the list of all sessions, and place it at
432|        # the end of the queue.
433|        for s in self._all_sessions:
434|            if s == session or s.name == session or session in s.signatures:  # noqa: PLR1714
435|                if posargs is not None:
436|                    s.posargs = list(posargs)
437|                self._queue.append(s)
438|                return True
439|
440|        # The session was not found in the list of sessions.
441|        msg = f"Session {session} not found."
442|        raise ValueError(msg)

445|class KeywordLocals(Mapping[str, bool]):
446|    """Eval locals using keywords.
447|
448|    When looking up a local variable the variable name is compared against
449|    the set of keywords. If the local variable name matches any *substring* of
450|    any keyword, then the name lookup returns True. Otherwise, the name lookup
451|    returns False.
452|    """
453|
454|    def __init__(self, keywords: Iterable[str]) -> None:
455|        self._keywords = frozenset(keywords)
456|
457|    def __getitem__(self, variable_name: str) -> bool:
458|        return any(variable_name in keyword for keyword in self._keywords)
459|
460|    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[str]:
461|        return iter(self._keywords)
462|
463|    def __len__(self) -> int:
464|        return len(self._keywords)
465|

467|def keyword_match(expression: str, keywords: Iterable[str]) -> Any:
468|    """See if an expression matches the given set of keywords."""
469|    # TODO: see if we can use ast.literal_eval here.
470|    my_locals = KeywordLocals(set(keywords))
471|    return eval(expression, {}, my_locals)  # noqa: S307

479|def _normalized_session_match(session_name: str, session: SessionRunner) -> bool:
480|    """Checks if session_name matches session."""
481|    if session_name == session.name or session_name in session.signatures:
482|        return True
483|    normalized_name = _normalize_arg(session_name)
484|    for name in session.signatures:
485|        equal_rep = normalized_name == _normalize_arg(name)
486|        if equal_rep:
487|            return True
488|    # Exhausted
489|    return False

41|def _copy_func(src: T, name: str | None = None) -> T:
42|    """This function copies another function, optionally with a new name."""
43|
44|    dst = types.FunctionType(
45|        src.__code__,

49|        closure=src.__closure__,

143|class Call(Func):
144|    """This represents a call of a function with a particular set of arguments."""
145|
146|    def __init__(self, func: Func, param_spec: Param) -> None:
147|        call_spec = param_spec.call_spec
148|        session_signature = f"({param_spec})"
149|
150|        # Determine the Python interpreter for the session using either @session
151|        # or @parametrize. For backwards compatibility, we only use a "python"
152|        # parameter in @parametrize if the session function does not expect it
153|        # as a normal argument, and if the @session decorator does not already
154|        # specify `python`.
155|
156|        python = func.python
157|        if python is None and "python" in call_spec:
158|            signature = inspect.signature(func.func)
159|            if "python" not in signature.parameters:
160|                python = call_spec.pop("python")
161|
162|        super().__init__(
163|            func,
164|            python,
165|            func.reuse_venv,
166|            None,
167|            func.venv_backend,
168|            func.venv_params,
169|            func.should_warn,
170|            func.tags + param_spec.tags,
171|            default=func.default,
172|            requires=func.requires,
173|            download_python=func.download_python,
174|            allow_parallel=func.allow_parallel,
175|        )
176|        self.call_spec = call_spec
177|        self.session_signature = session_signature
178|
179|    def __repr__(self) -> str:
180|        return f"{self.__class__.__name__}(name={self.name!r}, call_spec={self.call_spec!r}, session_signature={self.session_signature!r})"
181|
182|    def __call__(self, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
183|        kwargs.update(self.call_spec)
184|        return super().__call__(*args, **kwargs)
185|
186|    @classmethod
187|    def generate_calls(
188|        cls: type[Call], func: Func, param_specs: Iterable[Param]
189|    ) -> list[Call]:
190|        """Generates a list of calls based on the function and parameters."""
191|
192|        return [cls(func, param_spec) for param_spec in param_specs]

143|def run(
144|    args: Sequence[str | os.PathLike[str]],
145|    *,
146|    env: Mapping[str, str | None] | None = None,
147|    silent: bool = False,
148|    paths: Sequence[str | os.PathLike[str]] | None = None,
149|    success_codes: Iterable[int] | None = None,
150|    log: bool = True,
151|    external: ExternalType = False,
152|    stdout: int | IO[str] | None = None,
153|    stderr: int | IO[str] | None = subprocess.STDOUT,
154|    interrupt_timeout: float | None = DEFAULT_INTERRUPT_TIMEOUT,
155|    terminate_timeout: float | None = DEFAULT_TERMINATE_TIMEOUT,
156|) -> str | bool:
157|    """Run a command-line program."""
158|
159|    if success_codes is None:
160|        success_codes = [0]
161|
162|    cmd, args = args[0], args[1:]
163|    full_cmd = f"{cmd} {_shlex_join(args)}"
164|
165|    cmd_path = which(os.fspath(cmd), paths)
166|    str_args = [os.fspath(arg) for arg in args]
167|
168|    if log:
169|        logger.info(full_cmd)
170|
171|    abs_cmd_path = Path(os.path.abspath(cmd_path))
172|    is_external_tool = paths is not None and not any(
173|        abs_cmd_path.is_relative_to(os.path.abspath(path)) for path in paths
174|    )
175|    if is_external_tool:
176|        if external == "error":
177|            logger.error(
178|                f"Error: {cmd} is not installed into the virtualenv, it is located"
179|                f" at {cmd_path}. Pass external=True into run() to explicitly allow"
180|                " this."
181|            )
182|            msg = "External program disallowed."
183|            raise CommandFailed(msg)
184|        if external is False and log:
185|            logger.warning(
186|                f"Warning: {cmd} is not installed into the virtualenv, it is"
187|                f" located at {cmd_path}. This might cause issues! Pass"
188|                " external=True into run() to silence this message."
189|            )
190|
191|    env = _clean_env(env)
192|
193|    try:
194|        return_code, output = popen(
195|            [cmd_path, *str_args],
196|            silent=silent,
197|            env=env,
198|            stdout=stdout,
199|            stderr=stderr,
200|            interrupt_timeout=interrupt_timeout,
201|            terminate_timeout=terminate_timeout,
202|        )
203|
204|        if return_code not in success_codes:
205|            suffix = ":" if (silent and output) else ""
206|            logger.error(
207|                f"Command {full_cmd} failed with exit code {return_code}{suffix}"
208|            )
209|
210|            if silent and output:
211|                logger.error(output)
212|
213|            msg = f"Returned code {return_code}"
214|            raise CommandFailed(msg, return_code=return_code)
215|
216|        if output:
217|            logger.output(output)
218|
219|    except KeyboardInterrupt:
220|        logger.error("Interrupted...")
221|        raise
222|
223|    return output if silent else True

68|def _expandable_reference(arg: str, env: Mapping[str, str]) -> str | None:
69|    """Find a ``%VAR%`` reference that cmd.exe would expand, if there is one.
70|
71|    cmd.exe scans the text between each pair of ``%`` characters; when it
72|    names a defined (or dynamic) variable - optionally followed by ``:``
73|    modifiers, the value is substituted, even inside double quotes. An
74|    undefined name is left alone and the scan resumes at the trailing ``%``.
75|    """
76|    defined = {name.upper() for name in env}
77|    percents = [index for index, char in enumerate(arg) if char == "%"]
78|    for start, end in itertools.pairwise(percents):
79|        name = arg[start + 1 : end].partition(":")[0].upper()
80|        if name and (
81|            name in defined
82|            or name in _CMD_AUTO_VARS
83|            # hidden variables such as the per-drive working directory "=C:"
84|            or name.startswith("=")
85|        ):
86|            return arg[start : end + 1]
87|    return None

90|def _windows_batch_command(
91|    args: Sequence[str], env: Mapping[str, str] | None = None
92|) -> str:
93|    """Build a command line that protects the cmd.exe metacharacters ``&<>^|()``.
94|
95|    Arguments cmd.exe would corrupt anyway are rejected: ``%VAR%`` references
96|    are expanded even inside double quotes, and quote characters cannot be
97|    escaped. cmd.exe doesn't have backslash escapes, it only counts quotes.
98|    """
99|    if env is None:
100|        env = os.environ
101|
102|    quoted_args = []
103|    for arg in args:
104|        reference = _expandable_reference(arg, env)
105|        if reference is not None:
106|            msg = (
107|                "Cannot escape argument for batch script, cmd.exe would"
108|                f" expand {reference}: {arg}"
109|            )
110|            raise ValueError(msg)
111|        if _CMD_META.isdisjoint(arg):
112|            quoted_args.append(subprocess.list2cmdline([arg]))
113|        elif len(arg) >= 2 and arg[0] == arg[-1] == '"' and '"' not in arg[1:-1]:
114|            # A pre-quoted argument such as '"urllib3<1.25"' (the historical
115|            # workaround): its outer quotes already protect the
116|            # metacharacters, so pass it through unchanged.
117|            quoted_args.append(arg)
118|        elif '"' in arg:
119|            # list2cmdline escapes embedded quotes with backslashes, but
120|            # cmd.exe doesn't have backslash escapes.
121|            msg = f"Cannot escape argument for batch script: {arg}"
122|            raise ValueError(msg)
123|        else:
124|            # Force list2cmdline to quote the argument, then remove the
125|            # temporary leading space without changing the argument itself:
126|            # ' requests<99' -> '" requests<99"' -> '"requests<99"'
127|            quoted = subprocess.list2cmdline([f" {arg}"])
128|            quoted_args.append(f"{quoted[0]}{quoted[2:]}")
129|    return " ".join(quoted_args)

132|def shutdown_process(
133|    proc: subprocess.Popen[bytes],
134|    interrupt_timeout: float | None,
135|    terminate_timeout: float | None,
136|) -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
137|    """Gracefully shutdown a child process."""
138|    with contextlib.suppress(subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
139|        return proc.communicate(timeout=interrupt_timeout)
140|
141|    proc.terminate()
142|
143|    with contextlib.suppress(subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
144|        return proc.communicate(timeout=terminate_timeout)
145|
146|    proc.kill()
147|
148|    return proc.communicate()

151|def decode_output(output: bytes) -> str:
152|    """Try to decode the given bytes with encodings from the system.
153|
154|    :param output: output to decode
155|    :raises UnicodeDecodeError: if all encodings fail
156|    :return: decoded string
157|    """
158|    try:
159|        return output.decode("utf-8")
160|    except UnicodeDecodeError:
161|        second_encoding = locale.getpreferredencoding()
162|        if second_encoding.casefold() in {"utf8", "utf-8"}:
163|            raise
164|
165|        return output.decode(second_encoding)

175|    interrupt_timeout: float | None = DEFAULT_INTERRUPT_TIMEOUT,
176|    terminate_timeout: float | None = DEFAULT_TERMINATE_TIMEOUT,
177|) -> tuple[int, str]:
178|    if silent and stdout is not None:
179|        msg = (
180|            "Can not specify silent and stdout; passing a custom stdout always silences"
181|            " the commands output in Nox's log."
182|        )
183|        raise ValueError(msg)
184|
185|    if silent:
186|        stdout = subprocess.PIPE
187|
188|    popen_args: Sequence[str] | str = args
189|    if sys.platform.startswith("win") and args[0].casefold().endswith((".bat", ".cmd")):
190|        popen_args = _windows_batch_command(args, env)

200|        if proc.returncode != 0:

204|
205|    return return_code, decode_output(out) if out else ""

37|def lazy_stable_topo_sort(
38|    dependencies: Mapping[Node, Iterable[Node]],
39|    root: Node,
40|    *,
41|    drop_root: bool = True,
42|) -> Iterator[Node]:
43|    """Returns the "lazy, stable" topological sort of a dependency graph.
44|
45|    The sort returned will be a topological sort of the subgraph containing only
46|    ``root`` and its (recursive) dependencies. ``root`` will not be included in the
47|    output sort if ``drop_root`` is ``True``.
48|
49|    The sort returned is "lazy" in the sense that a node will not appear any earlier in
50|    the output sort than is necessitated by its dependents.
51|
52|    The sort returned is "stable" in the sense that the relative order of two nodes in
53|    ``dependencies[node]`` is preserved in the output sort, except when doing so would
54|    prevent the output sort from being either topological or lazy. The order of nodes in
55|    ``dependencies[node]`` allows the caller to exert a preference on the order of the
56|    output sort.
57|
58|    For example, consider:
59|
60|    >>> list(
61|    ...     lazy_stable_topo_sort(
62|    ...         dependencies = {
63|    ...             "a": ["c", "b"],
64|    ...             "b": [],
65|    ...             "c": [],
66|    ...             "d": ["e"],
67|    ...             "e": ["c"],
68|    ...             "root": ["a", "d"],
69|    ...         },
70|    ...         "root",
71|    ...         drop_root=False,
72|    ...     )
73|    ... )
74|    ["c", "b", "a", "e", "d", "root"]
75|
76|    Notice that:
77|
78|        1.  This is a topological sort of the dependency graph. That is, nodes only
79|            occur in the sort after all of their dependencies occur.
80|
81|        2.  Had we also included a node ``"f": ["b"]`` but kept ``dependencies["root"]``
82|            the same, the output would not have changed. This is because ``"f"`` was not
83|            requested directly by including it in ``dependencies["root"]`` or
84|            transitively as a (recursive) dependency of a node in
85|            ``dependencies["root"]``.
86|
87|        3.  ``"e"`` occurs no earlier than was required by its dependents ``{"d"}``.
88|            This is an example of the sort being "lazy". If ``"e"`` had occurred in the
89|            output any earlier---for example, just before ``"a"``---the sort would not
90|            have been lazy, but (in this example) the output would still have been a
91|            topological sort.
92|
93|        4.  Because the topological order between ``"a"`` and ``"d"`` is undefined and
94|            because it is possible to do so without making the output sort non-lazy,
95|            ``"a"`` and ``"d"`` are kept in the relative order that they have in
96|            ``dependencies["root"]``. This is an example of the sort being stable
97|            between pairs in ``dependencies[node]`` whenever possible. If ``"a"``'s
98|            dependency list was instead ``["d"]``, however, the relative order between
99|            ``"a"`` and ``"d"`` in ``dependencies["root"]`` would have been ignored to
100|            satisfy this dependency.
101|
102|            Similarly, ``"b"`` and ``"c"`` are kept in the relative order that they have
103|            in ``dependencies["a"]``. If ``"c"``'s dependency list was instead
104|            ``["b"]``, however, the relative order between ``"b"`` and ``"c"`` in
105|            ``dependencies["a"]`` would have been ignored to satisfy this dependency.
106|
107|    This implementation of this function is recursive and thus should not be used on
108|    large dependency graphs, but it is suitable for noxfile-sized dependency graphs.
109|
110|    Args:
111|        dependencies (Mapping[~nox._resolver.Node, Iterable[~nox._resolver.Node]]):
112|            A mapping from each node in the graph to the (ordered) list of nodes that it
113|            depends on. Using a mapping type with O(1) lookup (e.g. `dict`) is strongly
114|            suggested.
115|        root (~nox._resolver.Node):
116|            The root node to start the sort at. If ``drop_root`` is not ``True``,
117|            ``root`` will be the last element of the output.
118|        drop_root (bool):
119|            If ``True``, ``root`` will be not be included in the output sort. Defaults
120|            to ``True``.
121|
122|
123|    Returns:
124|        Iterator[~nox._resolver.Node]: The "lazy, stable" topological sort of the
125|        subgraph containing ``root`` and its dependencies.
126|
127|    Raises:
128|        ~nox._resolver.CycleError: If a dependency cycle is encountered.
129|    """
130|
131|    visited = dict.fromkeys(dependencies, False)
132|
133|    def prepended_by_dependencies(
134|        node: Node,
135|        walk: dict[Node, None] | None = None,
136|    ) -> Iterator[Node]:
137|        """Yields a node's dependencies depth-first, followed by the node itself.
138|
139|        A dependency will be skipped if has already been yielded by another call of
140|        ``prepended_by_dependencies``. Since ``prepended_by_dependencies`` is recursive,
141|        this means that each node will only be yielded once, and only the deepest
142|        occurrence of a node will be yielded.
143|
144|        Args:
145|            node (~nox._resolver.Node):
146|                A node in the dependency graph.
147|            walk (dict[~nox._resolver.Node, None] | None):
148|                An ordered ``dict`` whose keys are the nodes traversed when walking a
149|                path leading up to ``node`` on the reversed-edge dependency graph.
150|                Defaults to ``{}``.
151|
152|        Yields:
153|            ~nox._resolver.Node: ``node``'s direct dependencies, each
154|            prepended by their own direct dependencies, and so forth recursively,
155|            depth-first, followed by ``node``.
156|
157|        Raises:
158|            ValueError: If a dependency cycle is encountered.
159|        """
160|        # We would like for ``walk`` to be an ordered set so that we get (a) O(1) ``node
161|        # in walk`` and (b) so that we can use the order to report to the user what the
162|        # dependency cycle is, if one is encountered. The standard library does not have
163|        # an ordered set type, so we instead use the keys of an ``dict[Node, None]`` as
164|        # an ordered set.
165|        walk = walk or {}
166|        walk = extend_walk(walk, node)
167|        if not visited[node]:
168|            visited[node] = True
169|            # Recurse for each node in dependencies[node] in order so that we adhere to
170|            # the ``dependencies[node]`` order preference if doing so is possible.
171|            yield from itertools.chain.from_iterable(
172|                prepended_by_dependencies(dependency, walk)
173|                for dependency in dependencies[node]
174|            )
175|            yield node
176|
177|    def extend_walk(walk: dict[Node, None], node: Node) -> dict[Node, None]:
178|        """Extend a walk by a node, checking for dependency cycles.
179|
180|        Args:
181|            walk (dict[~nox._resolver.Node, None]):
182|                See ``prepended_by_dependencies``.
183|            nodes (~nox._resolver.Node):
184|                A node to extend the walk with.
185|
186|        Returns:
187|            dict[~nox._resolver.Node, None]: ``walk``, extended by
188|            ``node``.
189|
190|        Raises:
191|            ValueError: If extending ``walk`` by ``node`` introduces a cycle into the
192|                represented walk on the dependency graph.
193|        """
194|        walk = walk.copy()
195|        if node in walk:
196|            # Dependency cycle found.
197|            walk_list = list(walk)
198|            cycle = [*walk_list[walk_list.index(node) :], node]
199|            msg = "Nodes are in a dependency cycle"
200|            raise CycleError(msg, tuple(cycle))
201|        walk[node] = None
202|        return walk
203|
204|    sort = prepended_by_dependencies(root)
205|    if drop_root:
206|        return (node for node in sort if node != root)
207|    return sort

115|def sync(
116|    prefix: str,
117|    specs: Sequence[str],
118|    channels: Sequence[str],
119|    *,
120|    offline: bool = False,
121|) -> None:
122|    """Add ``specs`` to the requested set of ``prefix`` and bring it up to date.
123|
124|    Creates the prefix if it does not exist. Specs requested by earlier calls
125|    are kept unless the same package is requested again, so this behaves like
126|    ``conda install --prefix``.

132|        rattler.PrefixRecord.from_path(path)
133|        for path in sorted(Path(prefix, "conda-meta").glob("*.json"))
134|    ]
135|    new_specs = [rattler.MatchSpec(spec) for spec in specs]
136|    new_names = {ms.name.normalized for ms in new_specs}
137|    # A new request for a package replaces every historical request for it.
138|    # All specs from the current call are kept so `pkg>=2` and `pkg<3` both
139|    # reach the solver.
140|    match_specs = [
141|        ms
142|        for record in installed
143|        for spec in record.requested_specs or ()
144|        for ms in (rattler.MatchSpec(spec),)
145|        if ms.name.normalized not in new_names
146|    ]
147|    match_specs.extend(new_specs)
148|
149|    async def run() -> None:
150|        records = await rattler.solve(
151|            list(channels),
152|            match_specs,
153|            gateway=_gateway(offline=offline),
154|            virtual_packages=rattler.VirtualPackage.detect(),
155|            locked_packages=installed,
156|        )
157|        await rattler.install(
158|            records,
159|            prefix,
160|            installed_packages=installed,
161|            show_progress=False,
162|            # py-rattler passes this to the FFI unchanged, which wants the
163|            # inner object rather than the wrapper.
164|            requested_specs=[ms._match_spec for ms in match_specs],
165|            # Link scripts run unsandboxed; a user config must not enable them.
166|            execute_link_scripts=False,
167|            client=_client(),
168|            config=_config(),
169|        )
170|
171|    asyncio.run(run())

63|                        attr="needs_version",
64|                    ),
65|                    *_,
66|                ],
67|                value=ast.Constant(value=str() as constant_value),
68|            ):
69|                value = constant_value

248|                budget = width - 1 - len(head) - 2  # 2 for the separating spaces
249|                preview = preview[:budget] if budget > 0 else ""
250|            line = " ".join(_c(text, *codes) for text, codes in segments)
251|            if preview:
252|                line += f"  {_c(preview, 'thin')}"
253|            lines.append(line)
254|        return lines

256|    def _run(self) -> None:  # pragma: no cover - timing/terminal loop
257|        while not self._stop.wait(0.25):
258|            with self._lock:
259|                self._spin += 1
260|                self._draw_board()
261|
262|    def _draw_board(self) -> None:  # pragma: no cover - requires a live TTY
263|        self._clear_board()
264|        width = shutil.get_terminal_size().columns
265|        lines = self._render(time.monotonic(), width)
266|        for line in lines:
267|            self._write(line + "\n")
268|        self.stream.flush()
269|        self._board_lines = len(lines)
270|
271|    def _clear_board(self) -> None:
272|        if self._board_lines:  # pragma: no cover - requires a live TTY
273|            self.stream.write(f"\x1b[{self._board_lines}A\x1b[J")
274|            self.stream.flush()
275|            self._board_lines = 0

277|    def _emit_block(self, name: str, result: Result, output: str) -> None:
278|        symbol = _status_symbol(result.status, self.stream.encoding)
279|        duration = _duration_str(result.duration, ", {time}")
280|        rule = "=" * 10
281|        self._write(
282|            f"{rule} {symbol} {name}: {result.status.name.lower()}{duration} {rule}\n"
283|        )
284|        if output:
285|            self._write(output if output.endswith("\n") else output + "\n")
286|        elif result.reason:
287|            self._write(f"  {result.reason}\n")
288|        self.stream.flush()

290|    def started(self, name: str) -> None:
291|        with self._lock:
292|            self._active[name] = time.monotonic()
293|            if self.tty:  # pragma: no cover - requires a live TTY
294|                self._draw_board()
295|            else:
296|                self._write(f"Starting session {name}...\n")
297|                self.stream.flush()

299|    def update(self, name: str, line: str) -> None:
300|        """Record a session's latest output line for the status-board preview."""
301|        preview = _preview_text(line)
302|        if preview:
303|            with self._lock:
304|                self._preview[name] = preview
305|
306|    def finished(self, name: str, result: Result, output: str) -> None:
307|        with self._lock:
308|            self._active.pop(name, None)
309|            self._preview.pop(name, None)
310|            if result.status is Status.SKIPPED:
311|                self._skipped += 1
312|            elif result:
313|                self._passed += 1
314|            else:
315|                self._failed += 1
316|            self._clear_board()
317|            self._emit_block(name, result, output)
318|            if self.tty:  # pragma: no cover - requires a live TTY
319|                self._draw_board()

327|    field is resolved once, not on each scheduling pass.

336|def _session_selector(session: SessionRunner) -> str:
337|    """Return an unambiguous ``-s`` value selecting exactly this session.
338|
339|    ``friendly_name`` can be shared by several runners: with ``--force-python``,
340|    parametrized sessions for different interpreters all get e.g. ``test(x=1)``
341|    as their first signature. The fully-qualified signature (name, interpreter,
342|    and parameters, e.g. ``test-3.10(x=1)``) is unique, and is always the
343|    longest one a runner has.
344|    """
345|    return max(session.signatures, key=len) if session.signatures else session.name

348|def _child_argv(
349|    global_config: NoxConfig, session: SessionRunner, report_path: str
350|) -> list[str]:
351|    """Build the ``nox`` command line that runs a single session in a child.
352|
353|    The config is serialized back into arguments with ``to_argv``, so every
354|    option is forwarded by its declared ``Forward`` policy and new options
355|    reach children without changes here. The copy keeps the parent's value
356|    provenance (``attrs.evolve`` would reset it, silently dropping explicit
357|    CLI values that equal a field default); only the child-specific overrides
358|    (select exactly this session, run it alone, report to a file) are applied
359|    on top.
360|    """
361|    child_config = copy.deepcopy(global_config)
362|    overrides: dict[str, object] = {
363|        "sessions": [_session_selector(session)],
364|        "keywords": None,
365|        "tags": None,
366|        "parallel": 1,
367|        "parallel_worker": True,
368|        "no_dependencies": True,
369|        "report": report_path,
370|    }
371|    for name, value in overrides.items():
372|        child_config.set_value(name, value, _option_set.Source.COMMAND_LINE)
373|    return [sys.executable, "-m", "nox", *_option_set.to_argv(child_config)]

376|def _read_report(path: str, session: SessionRunner, returncode: int) -> Result:
377|    """Reconstruct a ``Result`` from a child's ``--report`` file."""
378|    try:
379|        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as report_file:
380|            entry = json.load(report_file)["sessions"][0]
381|        result = Result.from_dict(session, entry)
382|    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, IndexError):
383|        # The child died before writing a usable report; trust its exit code.
384|        status = Status.SUCCESS if returncode == 0 else Status.FAILED
385|        return Result(session, status)
386|    # A child may run more than the scheduled session (e.g. via notify()); its
387|    # exit code reflects every one of them. Don't report success over a non-zero
388|    # child whose first session happened to pass.
389|    if returncode != 0 and result:
390|        return Result(session, Status.FAILED, duration=result.duration)
391|    return result

394|class _Children:
395|    """The child processes that are running right now.
396|
397|    Each session's child is registered for as long as it runs, so an interrupt
398|    in the main thread can stop whatever is running at that moment.
399|    """
400|
401|    def __init__(self) -> None:
402|        self._lock = threading.Lock()
403|        self._procs: set[subprocess.Popen[bytes]] = set()
404|
405|    @contextlib.contextmanager
406|    def spawn(
407|        self, argv: list[str], cwd: str | None
408|    ) -> Iterator[subprocess.Popen[bytes]]:
409|        """Start a session's child process, tracked for as long as it runs."""
410|        # The context manager waits for the process and closes its pipes.
411|        with subprocess.Popen(
412|            argv,
413|            cwd=cwd,
414|            # Detach stdin so the child never sees a TTY: parallel sessions
415|            # must not prompt or read from the shared terminal (they would
416|            # race/hang).
417|            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
418|            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
419|            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
420|            # Own process group (POSIX) so an interrupt can stop the whole
421|            # tree, including the session's own subprocesses.
422|            start_new_session=(os.name == "posix"),
423|        ) as proc:
424|            with self._lock:
425|                self._procs.add(proc)
426|            try:
427|                yield proc
428|            finally:
429|                with self._lock:
430|                    self._procs.discard(proc)
431|
432|    def stop_all(self) -> None:
433|        with self._lock:
434|            running = list(self._procs)
435|        _stop_procs(running)

437|
438|def _run_session(
439|    session: SessionRunner,
440|    global_config: NoxConfig,
441|    children: _Children,
442|    on_line: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
443|) -> tuple[Result, str]:
444|    """Run a single session in a subprocess; return its result and output.
445|
446|    Output is read line by line so ``on_line`` (if given) sees each line as it
447|    arrives, letting the caller show a live preview while the session runs.
448|    """
449|    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
450|        report_path = os.path.join(tmp, "report.json")
451|        lines: list[str] = []
452|        with children.spawn(
453|            _child_argv(global_config, session, report_path),
454|            global_config.invoked_from,
455|        ) as proc:
456|            assert proc.stdout is not None
457|            # newline="" splits at \r too but doesn't translate it, so
458|            # progress-bar redraws stay overwrites instead of becoming
459|            # separate lines in the buffered block.
460|            reader = io.TextIOWrapper(
461|                proc.stdout,
462|                encoding="utf-8",
463|                errors="backslashreplace",
464|                newline="",
465|            )
466|            for raw_line in iter(reader.readline, ""):
467|                line = f"{raw_line[:-2]}\n" if raw_line.endswith("\r\n") else raw_line
468|                lines.append(line)
469|                if on_line is not None:
470|                    on_line(line)
471|        return _read_report(report_path, session, proc.returncode), "".join(lines)

474|def _signal_group(proc: subprocess.Popen[bytes], *, kill: bool) -> None:
475|    """Signal a child's whole process group (POSIX), or just the child."""
476|    if os.name == "posix":
477|        with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError, PermissionError):
478|            os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL if kill else signal.SIGTERM)
479|        return
480|    (proc.kill if kill else proc.terminate)()  # pragma: no cover - Windows
481|
482|
483|def _stop_procs(procs: Collection[subprocess.Popen[bytes]]) -> None:
484|    """Terminate the children (and their process groups, so the sessions' own
485|    subprocesses stop too), escalating to SIGKILL for any that don't exit."""
486|    for proc in procs:
487|        _signal_group(proc, kill=False)
488|    deadline = time.monotonic() + _TERMINATE_TIMEOUT
489|    for proc in procs:
490|        try:
491|            proc.wait(timeout=max(0.0, deadline - time.monotonic()))
492|        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:  # noqa: PERF203 - cold shutdown path
493|            _signal_group(proc, kill=True)

496|def run_manifest_parallel(
497|    manifest: Manifest, global_config: NoxConfig, jobs: int
498|) -> list[Result]:
499|    """Run the manifest's sessions concurrently, honoring ``requires=``.
500|
501|    Args:
502|        manifest: The (already filtered and dependency-resolved) manifest.
503|        global_config: The global configuration.
504|        jobs: The maximum number of sessions to run at once.
505|
506|    Returns:
507|        The results, in manifest order, for every session that ran.
508|    """
509|    queue = list(manifest)
510|    in_queue = set(queue)
511|    nodes = [
512|        _Node(
513|            session=session,
514|            deps=[d for d in session.get_direct_dependencies() if d in in_queue],
515|            # envdir is a nontrivial property (path normalization, possibly a
516|            # hashing warning); compute it once instead of on every pass.
517|            envdir=session.envdir,
518|            allow_parallel=resolve_allow_parallel(global_config, session.func),
519|        )
520|        for session in queue
521|    ]
522|
523|    results: dict[SessionRunner, Result] = {}
524|    not_started = list(nodes)
525|    futures: dict[Future[Result], _Node] = {}
526|    children = _Children()
527|    stop = False
528|
529|    reporter = _Reporter(
530|        color=bool(global_config.color),
531|        tty=sys.stdout.isatty(),
532|        total=len(queue),
533|    )
534|
535|    def worker(node: _Node) -> Result:
536|        name = node.session.friendly_name
537|        reporter.started(name)
538|        result, output = _run_session(
539|            node.session,
540|            global_config,
541|            children,
542|            # The preview only feeds the TTY status board; skip the per-line
543|            # work entirely when there isn't one.
544|            on_line=(lambda line: reporter.update(name, line))
545|            if reporter.tty
546|            else None,
547|        )
548|        reporter.finished(name, result, output)
549|        return result
550|
551|    def schedule_ready(executor: ThreadPoolExecutor) -> None:
552|        """Submit ready sessions, up to ``jobs`` running at once.
553|
554|        A session is ready once all its dependencies have completed. Sessions
555|        with a failed/aborted/skipped prerequisite are aborted in place
556|        (without spawning a subprocess and regardless of capacity), which
557|        cascades down the graph. Sessions sharing an envdir (runners with
558|        duplicated friendly names under ``--force-python``) are never run at
559|        the same time, as they would build the same virtualenv concurrently.
560|        Sessions that don't allow parallel execution run exclusively: they
561|        start only when nothing else is running, and nothing starts alongside
562|        them.
563|        """
564|        busy_envdirs = {running.envdir for running in futures.values()}
565|        exclusive_running = any(
566|            not running.allow_parallel for running in futures.values()
567|        )
568|        # The fixpoint loop is load-bearing: when a failure cascades while
569|        # nothing is running, every transitive dependent must be aborted in
570|        # this call, because the main loop exits once no futures remain.
571|        progressed = True
572|        while progressed:
573|            progressed = False
574|            for node in list(not_started):
575|                if not all(dep in results for dep in node.deps):
576|                    continue
577|                failed = [dep for dep in node.deps if not results[dep]]
578|                if failed:
579|                    not_started.remove(node)
580|                    progressed = True
581|                    result = Result.aborted_prerequisite(node.session, failed[0])
582|                    results[node.session] = result
583|                    reporter.finished(node.session.friendly_name, result, "")
584|                elif (
585|                    len(futures) < jobs
586|                    and not exclusive_running
587|                    and node.envdir not in busy_envdirs
588|                    and (node.allow_parallel or not futures)
589|                ):
590|                    not_started.remove(node)
591|                    progressed = True
592|                    busy_envdirs.add(node.envdir)
593|                    exclusive_running = not node.allow_parallel
594|                    futures[executor.submit(worker, node)] = node
595|
596|    start = time.monotonic()
597|    with reporter, ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=jobs) as executor:
598|        try:
599|            while True:
600|                if not stop:
601|                    schedule_ready(executor)
602|                if not futures:
603|                    break
604|                done, _ = wait(futures, return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED)
605|                for future in done:
606|                    node = futures.pop(future)
607|                    result = future.result()
608|                    results[node.session] = result
609|                    if not result and global_config.stop_on_first_error:
610|                        stop = True
611|        except KeyboardInterrupt:  # pragma: no cover - hard to trigger in tests
612|            children.stop_all()
613|            executor.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)
614|            raise
615|
616|    # Report wall-clock time in the summary, not the sum of session durations.
617|    global_config.parallel_wall_time = time.monotonic() - start
618|    return [results[session] for session in queue if session in results]

31|def execute(workflow: Iterable[Callable[..., Any]], global_config: NoxConfig) -> int:
32|    """Execute each function in the workflow.
33|
34|    Each function in the workflow receives the result of the previous one
35|    (if any) and the global configuration.
36|
37|    If any function returns an integer, it is considered to be an exit code.
38|    This means that the iteration of functions is aborted, and the exit code
39|    returned immediately.
40|
41|    This approach promotes testability and separation of concerns.
42|
43|    Args:
44|        workflow (Iterable[function]): The functions to be executed.
45|        global_config (~.GlobalConfig): The global configuration, which
46|            is passed to each task.
47|
48|    Returns:
49|        int: An exit code.
50|    """
51|    try:
52|        # Iterate over each task and run it.
53|        return_value: Any = None
54|        for function_ in workflow:
55|            # Send the previous task's return value if there was one.
56|            args: list[Any] = []
57|            if return_value is not None:
58|                args.append(return_value)
59|            kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"global_config": global_config}
60|            return_value = function_(*args, **kwargs)
61|
62|            # If we got an integer value as a result, abort task processing
63|            # and return it.
64|            if isinstance(return_value, int):
65|                return return_value
66|    except KeyboardInterrupt:
67|        return 130  # http://tldp.org/LDP/abs/html/exitcodes.html
68|
69|    # All tasks completed, presumably without error.
70|    return 0

77|    with open(filename, "w", encoding="utf-8") as outfile:
78|        outfile.write(output)
79|
80|
81|def main() -> None:
82|    make_parser = functools.partial(argparse.ArgumentParser, allow_abbrev=False)
83|    if sys.version_info >= (3, 14):
84|        make_parser = functools.partial(make_parser, color=True, suggest_on_error=True)
85|    parser = make_parser(description="Converts toxfiles to noxfiles.")
86|    parser.add_argument("--output", default="noxfile.py")
87|
88|    args = parser.parse_args()
89|
90|    output = check_output(["tox", "config"], text=True, encoding="utf-8")  # noqa: S607
91|    original_config = ConfigParser()
92|    original_config.read_string(output)
93|    config: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
94|
95|    for name, section in original_config.items():
96|        if name == "DEFAULT":
97|            continue
98|
99|        config[name] = dict(section)
100|        # Convert set_env from string to dict
101|        set_env = {}
102|        for var in section.get("set_env", "").strip().splitlines():
103|            k, v = var.split("=", 1)
104|            if k not in {
105|                "PYTHONHASHSEED",
106|                "PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK",
107|                "PYTHONIOENCODING",
108|                # Listed by tox 4.64.8+
109|                "PIP_USER",
110|                "TOX_ENV_DIR",
111|                "TOX_ENV_NAME",
112|                "TOX_WORK_DIR",
113|                "VIRTUAL_ENV",
114|            }:
115|                set_env[k] = v
116|
117|        config[name]["set_env"] = set_env
118|
119|        config[name]["commands"] = [
120|            wrapjoin(shlex.split(c)) for c in section["commands"].strip().splitlines()
121|        ]
122|
123|        config[name]["deps"] = wrapjoin(
124|            [
125|                part
126|                for dep in section["deps"].strip().splitlines()
127|                for part in (dep.split() if dep.startswith("-r") else [dep])
128|            ]
129|        )
130|
131|        for option in "skip_install", "use_develop":
132|            if section.get(option):
133|                config[name][option] = section[option] != "False"
134|
135|        if os.path.isabs(section["base_python"]) or re.match(
136|            r"py\d+", section["base_python"]
137|        ):
138|            impl = "python" if section["py_impl"] == "cpython" else section["py_impl"]
139|            config[name]["base_python"] = impl + section["py_dot_ver"]
140|
141|        change_dir = Path(section.get("change_dir", ""))
142|        try:
143|            rel_to_cwd = change_dir.relative_to(Path.cwd())
144|        except ValueError:
145|            # change_dir is outside the project root, keep the absolute path
146|            config[name]["change_dir"] = change_dir
147|        else:
148|            if str(rel_to_cwd) == ".":
149|                config[name]["change_dir"] = None
150|            else:
151|                config[name]["change_dir"] = rel_to_cwd
152|
153|    output = _TEMPLATE.render(config=config, wrapjoin=wrapjoin, fixname=fixname)
154|
155|    write_output_to_file(output, args.output)

1|# Changelog
2|
3|## 2026.10.20
4|
5|Parallel mode no longer prints an "experimental" banner, and sessions can check
6|`session.parallel` to see if they run in a parallel worker. A new `rattler`
7|backend uses py-rattler (install with the `nox[rattler]` extra), so you can
8|request fast conda-style environments in a `/// script` block. Python versions
9|read from classifiers now include free-threaded builds when the free-threading
10|classifier is present, and are deduplicated. A single-argument
11|`@nox.parametrize` now accepts ranges and other iterators, and the `rattler`
12|backend loads config from the default locations. The GitHub Action now
13|defaults to Python 3.11-3.15. This release also fixes several bugs in script
14|mode, option handling, and `tox-to-nox`.
15|
16|We'd like to thank the following folks who contributed to this release:
17|
18|* @henryiii
19|* @Himanshuagrawal4
