1|The Nox Cookbook
2|================
3|
4|The What?
5|---------
6|
7|A lot of people and a lot of projects use Nox for their python automation powers.
8|
9|Some of these sessions are the classic "run pytest and linting", some are more unique and more interesting!
10|
11|The Nox cookbook is a collection of these sessions.
12|
13|Nox is super easy to get started with, and super powerful right out of the box. But when things get complex or you want to chain together some more powerful tasks, often the only examples can be found hunting around GitHub for novel sessions.
14|
15|The kind of sessions that make you think "I didn't know you could do that!"
16|
17|This cookbook is intended to be a centralized, community-driven repository of awesome Nox sessions to act as a source of inspiration and a reference guide for Nox's users. If you're doing something cool with Nox, why not add your session here?
18|
19|
20|Contributing a Session
21|----------------------
22|
23|Anyone can contribute sessions to the cookbook. However, there are a few guiding principles you should keep in mind:
24|
25|* Your session should be interesting or unique, it should do something out of the ordinary or otherwise interesting.
26|* You should explain briefly what it does and why it's interesting.
27|
28|For general advice on how to contribute to Nox see our :doc:`CONTRIBUTING` guide
29|
30|Recipes
31|-------
32|
33|Instant Dev Environment
34|^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
35|
36|A common sticking point in contributing to python projects (especially for beginners) is the problem of wrangling virtual environments and installing dependencies.
37|
38|Enter the ``dev`` nox session:
39|
40|.. code-block:: python
41|
42|    import nox
43|
44|
45|    # It's a good idea to keep your dev session out of the default list
46|    # so it's not run twice accidentally
47|    @nox.session(default=False)
48|    def dev(session: nox.Session) -> None:
49|        """
50|        Set up a python development environment for the project at ".venv".
51|        """
52|
53|        session.install("virtualenv")
54|
55|        session.run("virtualenv", ".venv", silent=True)
56|
57|        # Use the venv's interpreter to install the project along with
58|        # all its dev dependencies, this ensures it's installed in the right way
59|        session.run(".venv/bin/pip", "install", "-e", ".[dev]", external=True)
60|
61|With this, a user can simply run ``nox -s dev`` and have their entire environment set up automatically!
62|
63|
64|The Auto-Release
65|^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
66|
67|Releasing a new version of an open source project can be a real pain, with lots of intricate steps. Tools like `Bump My Version <https://github.com/callowayproject/bump-my-version>`_ really help here.
68|
69|Even more so with a sprinkling of Nox:
70|
71|.. code-block:: python
72|
73|    import argparse
74|    import nox
75|
76|    @nox.session
77|    def release(session: nox.Session) -> None:
78|        """
79|        Kicks off an automated release process by creating and pushing a new tag.
80|
81|        Invokes bump-my-version with the posarg selecting the version part.
82|
83|        Usage:
84|        $ nox -s release -- [major|minor|patch]
85|        """
86|        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Release a semver version.")
87|        parser.add_argument(
88|            "version",
89|            type=str,
90|            nargs=1,
91|            help="The type of semver release to make.",
92|            choices={"major", "minor", "patch"},
93|        )
94|        args: argparse.Namespace = parser.parse_args(args=session.posargs)
95|        version: str = args.version.pop()
96|
97|        # If we get here, we should be good to go
98|        # Let's do a final check for safety
99|        confirm = input(
100|            f"You are about to bump the {version!r} version. Are you sure? [y/n]: "
101|        )
102|
103|        # Abort on anything other than 'y'
104|        if confirm.lower().strip() != "y":
105|            session.error(f"You said no when prompted to bump the {version!r} version.")
106|
107|
108|        session.install("bump-my-version")
109|
110|        session.log(f"Bumping the {version!r} version")
111|        session.run("bump-my-version", "bump", version)
112|
113|        session.log("Pushing the new tag")
114|        session.run("git", "push", external=True)
115|        session.run("git", "push", "--tags", external=True)
116|
117|Now a simple ``nox -s release -- patch`` will automate your release (provided you have Bump My Version set up to change your files). This is especially powerful if you have a CI/CD pipeline set up!
118|
119|
120|Using a lockfile
121|^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
122|
123|If you use a tool like ``uv`` to lock your dependencies, you can use that inside a nox session. Here's an example:
124|
125|.. code-block:: python
126|
127|    @nox.session(venv_backend="uv")
128|    def tests(session: nox.Session) -> None:
129|        """
130|        Run the unit and regular tests.
131|        """
132|        session.run_install(
133|            "uv",
134|            "sync",
135|            "--extra=test",
136|            "--no-default-extras",
137|            f"--python={session.virtualenv.location}",
138|            env={"UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT": session.virtualenv.location},
139|        )
140|        session.run("pytest", *session.posargs)
141|
142|
143|Here we run ``uv sync`` on the nox virtual environment. Other useful flags might include ``--locked`` (validate lockfile is up-to-date) and ``--inexact`` (will allow you to install other packages as well).
144|
145|The `nox-uv <https://github.com/dantebben/nox-uv>`_ package can be used to reduce the boilerplate needed to ``uv sync`` specific dependency groups or extras into the nox virtual environment.
146|By default, ``nox-uv`` also validates that the lockfile is up-to-date.
147|
148|.. code-block:: python
149|
150|    #!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script --quiet
151|
152|    # /// script
153|    # dependencies = ["nox", "nox-uv"]
154|    # ///
155|
156|    import nox
157|    import nox_uv
158|
159|    nox.options.default_venv_backend = "uv"
160|
161|    @nox_uv.session(
162|        python=["3.10", "3.11", "3.12", "3.13"],
163|        uv_groups=["test"],
164|    )
165|    def test(s: nox.Session) -> None:
166|        """`uv sync` main dependencies and the `test` dependency group."""
167|        s.run("python", "-m", "pytest")
168|
169|    @nox_uv.session(uv_groups=["type_check"])
170|    def type_check(s: nox.Session) -> None:
171|        """`uv sync` main dependencies and the `type_check` dependency group."""
172|        s.run("mypy", "src")
173|
174|    @nox_uv.session(uv_only_groups=["lint"])
175|    def lint(s: nox.Session) -> None:
176|        """`uv sync` only the `lint` dependency group."""
177|        s.run("ruff", "check", ".")
178|        s.run("ruff", "format", "--check", ".")
179|
180|
181|    if __name__ == "__main__":
182|        nox.main()
183|
184|
185|Testing on every supported Python
186|^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
187|
188|The ``Programming Language :: Python :: 3.X`` trove classifiers in
189|``pyproject.toml`` already list every Python your project supports.
190|:func:`nox.project.python_versions` reads them, so the session matrix follows
191|the classifiers without a second copy of the list. If the project also has a
192|``Programming Language :: Python :: Free Threading`` classifier, the
193|non-experimental free-threaded builds (``3.14t`` and newer) are added too:
194|
195|.. code-block:: toml
196|
197|    [project]
198|    classifiers = [
199|      "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
200|      "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
201|      "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
202|      "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.15",
203|      "Programming Language :: Python :: Free Threading :: 3 - Stable",
204|    ]
205|
206|.. code-block:: python
207|
208|    import nox
209|
210|    PYPROJECT = nox.project.load_toml("pyproject.toml")
211|    # ["3.12", "3.13", "3.14", "3.14t, "3.15", "3.15t"]
212|    ALL_PYTHON = nox.project.python_versions(PYPROJECT)
213|
214|
215|    @nox.session(python=ALL_PYTHON)
216|    def tests(session: nox.Session) -> None:
217|        session.install("-e.", "pytest")
218|        session.run("pytest")
219|
220|Pass ``free_threaded=False`` to leave the free-threaded builds out, or
221|``free_threaded=True`` to add them without the classifier. 3.13t is never
222|added automatically, as free threading was experimental in 3.13.
223|
224|
225|Combining coverage across Python versions
226|^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
227|
228|Code paths can vary between Python versions, so measuring each test run separately
229|and then combining the data gives a more accurate coverage report. The important
230|parts are to remove stale data before the matrix starts, give every run a unique
231|data file, and combine the files only after every test session finishes:
232|
233|.. code-block:: python
234|
235|    import nox
236|
237|    PYPROJECT = nox.project.load_toml("pyproject.toml")
238|    PYTHON_VERSIONS = nox.project.python_versions(PYPROJECT)
239|
240|
241|    @nox.session(default=False)
242|    def coverage_erase(session: nox.Session) -> None:
243|        """Remove data left by an earlier coverage run."""
244|        session.install("coverage[toml]")
245|        session.run("coverage", "erase")
246|
247|
248|    @nox.session(
249|        python=PYTHON_VERSIONS,
250|        default=False,
251|        requires=["coverage_erase"],
252|    )
253|    def tests(session: nox.Session) -> None:
254|        """Measure tests independently for each supported Python version."""
255|        session.install("coverage[toml]", "--group=test", ".")
256|        session.run(
257|            "coverage",
258|            "run",
259|            "-m",
260|            "pytest",
261|            *session.posargs,
262|            env={"COVERAGE_FILE": f".coverage.{session.python}"},
263|        )
264|
265|
266|    @nox.session(requires=["tests"])
267|    def coverage_report(session: nox.Session) -> None:
268|        """Combine the per-version data and display one report."""
269|        session.install("coverage[toml]")
270|        session.run("coverage", "combine")
271|        session.run("coverage", "report", "--show-missing")
272|
273|Running ``nox`` selects ``coverage_report`` by default; its requirements run
274|cleanup first and then every parametrized test session. ``coverage combine``
275|writes the combined ``.coverage`` data file and removes the per-version files it
276|consumed.
277|Keep the phases sequential so cleanup and reporting cannot race with the test
278|sessions. Projects that use subprocesses or pytest-xdist should also enable
279|Coverage.py's `parallel mode <https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config.html#run-parallel>`_.
280|
281|
282|Generating a matrix with GitHub Actions
283|^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
284|
285|Nox knows what sessions it needs to run. Why not tell GitHub Actions what jobs to run dynamically? Using the ``--json`` flag and a bit of json processing, it's easy:
286|
287|.. code-block:: yaml
288|
289|    jobs:
290|      generate-jobs:
291|        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
292|        outputs:
293|          session: ${{ steps.set-matrix.outputs.session }}
294|        steps:
295|        - uses: actions/checkout@v3
296|        - uses: wntrblm/nox@main
297|        - id: set-matrix
298|          shell: bash
299|          run: echo session=$(nox --json -l | jq -c '[.[].session]') | tee --append $GITHUB_OUTPUT
300|      checks:
301|        name: Session ${{ matrix.session }}
302|        needs: [generate-jobs]
303|        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
304|        strategy:
305|          fail-fast: false
306|          matrix:
307|            session: ${{ fromJson(needs.generate-jobs.outputs.session) }}
308|        steps:
309|        - uses: actions/checkout@v3
310|        - uses: wntrblm/nox@main
311|        - run: nox -s "${{ matrix.session }}"

1|Welcome to Nox
2|==============
3|

14|
15|``nox`` is a command-line tool that automates testing in multiple Python environments, similar to `tox`_. Unlike tox, Nox uses a standard Python file for configuration.
16|
17|To install Nox with `pipx`_::
18|
19|    pipx install nox
20|
21|You can also use `pip`_ in your global python::
22|
23|    python3 -m pip install nox
24|
25|
26|Nox is configured via a ``noxfile.py`` file in your project's directory. Here's a simple noxfile that runs lint and some tests::
27|
28|    import nox
29|
30|    @nox.session
31|    def tests(session):
32|        session.install('pytest')
33|        session.run('pytest')
34|
35|    @nox.session
36|    def lint(session):
37|        session.install('flake8')
38|        session.run('flake8', '--import-order-style', 'google')
39|
40|To run both of these sessions, just run::
41|
42|    nox
43|
44|For each session, Nox will automatically create an isolated environment with the appropriate Python interpreter using the configured :ref:`environment backend <virtualenv config>`, install the specified dependencies, and run the commands in order.
45|
46|To learn how to install and use Nox, see the :doc:`tutorial`. For documentation on configuring sessions, see :doc:`config`. For documentation on running ``nox``, see :doc:`usage`.
47|

89|Nox is not the only tool of its kind. If Nox doesn't quite fit your needs or you want to do more research, we recommend looking at these tools:

92|- `Invoke <https://www.pyinvoke.org/>`__ is a general-purpose task execution library, similar to Make. Nox can be thought of as if Invoke were tailored specifically to Python testing, so Invoke is a great choice for scripts that need to encompass far more than Nox's specialization.

14|
15|*Flexible test automation with Python*
16|
17|* **Documentation:** [https://nox.readthedocs.io](https://nox.readthedocs.io)
18|
19|* **Source Code:** [https://github.com/wntrblm/nox](https://github.com/wntrblm/nox)
20|
21|## Overview
22|
23|`nox` is a command-line tool that automates testing in multiple Python environments, similar to [tox][]. Unlike tox, Nox uses a standard Python file for configuration:
24|
25|```python
26|import nox
27|
28|
29|@nox.session
30|def tests(session: nox.Session) -> None:
31|    session.install("pytest")
32|    session.run("pytest")
33|
34|
35|@nox.session
36|def lint(session: nox.Session) -> None:
37|    session.install("flake8")
38|    session.run("flake8", "--import-order-style", "google")
39|```
40|
41|## Installation
42|
43|Nox is designed to be installed globally (not in a project virtual environment), the recommended way of doing this is via [pipx], a tool designed to install python CLI programs whilst keeping them separate from your global or system python.
44|
45|To install Nox with [pipx][]:
46|
47|```shell
48|pipx install nox
49|```
50|
51|You can also use [pip][] in your global python:
52|
53|```shell
54|python3 -m pip install nox
55|```
56|
57|You may want to use the [user-site][] to avoid messing with your Global python install:
58|
59|```shell
60|python3 -m pip install --user nox
61|```
62|
63|## Usage
64|
65|### List all sessions
66|
67|```shell
68|nox -l/--list
69|```
70|
71|### Get help on a particular session (if it has a docstring)
72|
73|```shell
74|nox --usage test
75|```
76|
77|### Run all sessions
78|
79|```shell
80|nox
81|```
82|
83|### Run a particular session
84|
85|```shell
86|nox -s/--session test
87|```
88|
89|Checkout the [docs](https://nox.readthedocs.io) for more! 🎉
90|
91|## Contributing
92|
93|Nox is an open source project and welcomes contributions of all kinds, checkout the [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) for help on how to help us out!
94|
95|All contributors must follow the [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) and be nice to one another! 😃
96|

99|[pip]: https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/

1|# Contributing
2|
3|Thank you for your interest in improving Nox. Nox is open-source under the
4|[Apache License Version 2.0](http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0) and welcomes contributions in the form of bug reports, feature requests, and pull requests.
5|
6|Nox is hosted on [GitHub](https://github.com/wntrblm/nox).
7|
8|## Support, questions, and feature requests
9|
10|Feel free to file a bug or feature request on [GitHub](https://github.com/wntrblm/nox). If your question is more general or does not fit neatly into one of those categories, we also have a Nox channel on the [Winterbloom Discord server](https://discord.com/invite/UpfqghQ).
11|
12|You should find a permalink to the invite when you raise a new issue on GitHub.
13|
14|## Reporting issues
15|
16|File a bug on [GitHub](https://github.com/wntrblm/nox). To help us figure out what's going on, please err on the
17|side of including lots of information, such as:
18|
19|* Operating system.
20|* Python version.
21|* If possible, a minimal case that can reproduce the issue.
22|
23|## Pull requests
24|
25|* It's recommended to file a bug before starting work on anything. It'll allow
26|  chance to talk it over with the owners and validate your approach.
27|* Nox maintains 100% test coverage. All pull requests must maintain this.
28|* Follow [pep8](https://pep8.org).
29|* Update documentation and tests if relevant.
30|* Ensure your changes pass Nox's tests and lint suites before pushing.
31|
32|## Running tests
33|
34|Nox runs its own tests (it's recursive!). The best thing to do is start with
35|a known-good Nox installation, e.g. from PyPI:
36|
37|    pip install --pre --upgrade nox
38|
39|To just check for lint errors, run:
40|
41|    nox --session lint
42|
43|To run against a particular Python version:
44|
45|    nox --session tests-3.12
46|    nox --session conda_tests
47|    nox --session mamba_tests
48|    nox --session micromamba_tests
49|
50|When you send a pull request the CI will handle running everything, but it is
51|recommended to test as much as possible locally before pushing.
52|
53|You can list all possible tests with:
54|
55|    nox --list-sessions
56|
57|## Getting a sticker
58|
59|If you've contributed to Nox, you can get a cute little Nox sticker. Reach out to Thea at me@thea.codes to request one.
60|
61|## Getting paid
62|
63|Contributions to Nox can be expensed through [our Open Collective](https://opencollective.com/python-nox). The maintainers will let you know when and for how much you can expense contributions, but always feel free to ask.

29|* Update documentation and tests if relevant.
30|* Ensure your changes pass Nox's tests and lint suites before pushing.
31|
32|## Running tests
33|
34|Nox runs its own tests (it's recursive!). The best thing to do is start with
35|a known-good Nox installation, e.g. from PyPI:
36|
37|    pip install --pre --upgrade nox
38|
39|To just check for lint errors, run:
40|
41|    nox --session lint
42|
43|To run against a particular Python version:
44|
45|    nox --session tests-3.12
46|    nox --session conda_tests
47|    nox --session mamba_tests
48|    nox --session micromamba_tests
49|
50|When you send a pull request the CI will handle running everything, but it is
51|recommended to test as much as possible locally before pushing.
52|
53|You can list all possible tests with:
54|
55|    nox --list-sessions
56|
57|## Getting a sticker
58|
59|If you've contributed to Nox, you can get a cute little Nox sticker. Reach out to Thea at me@thea.codes to request one.
60|
61|## Getting paid
62|
63|Contributions to Nox can be expensed through [our Open Collective](https://opencollective.com/python-nox). The maintainers will let you know when and for how much you can expense contributions, but always feel free to ask.

--- FILE: action.yml ---
1|name: Setup Nox
2|description: "Prepares all python versions for nox"
3|inputs:
4|  python-versions:
5|    description: "comma-separated list of python versions to install"
6|    required: false
7|    default: "3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14, 3.15"
8|branding:
9|  icon: package
10|  color: blue
11|
12|runs:
13|  using: composite
14|  steps:
15|    - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
16|      id: localpython
17|      with:
18|        python-version: "3.10 - 3.15"
19|        update-environment: false
20|
21|    - name: "Validate input"
22|      id: helper
23|      run: >
24|        "${STEPS_LOCALPYTHON_OUTPUTS_PYTHON_PATH}" "${{ github.action_path }}/.github/action_helper.py" "${INPUTS_PYTHON_VERSIONS}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
25|      shell: bash
26|      env:
27|        STEPS_LOCALPYTHON_OUTPUTS_PYTHON_PATH: ${{ steps.localpython.outputs.python-path }}
28|        INPUTS_PYTHON_VERSIONS: ${{ inputs.python-versions }}
29|
30|    - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
31|      id: allpython
32|      with:
33|        python-version: "${{ join(fromJSON(steps.helper.outputs.interpreters), '\n') }}"
34|        allow-prereleases: true
35|
36|    - name: "Install nox"
37|      run: |
38|        import os
39|        import shutil
40|        import sys
41|        import venv
42|
43|        from pathlib import Path
44|        from subprocess import run
45|
46|
47|        class EnvBuilder(venv.EnvBuilder):
48|            def __init__(self):
49|                super().__init__()
50|
51|            def setup_scripts(self, context):
52|                pass
53|
54|            def post_setup(self, context):
55|                super().post_setup(context)
56|                self.bin_path = Path(context.env_exe).parent
57|                if shutil.which("uv") is None:
58|                    run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "--python", context.env_exe, "install", r"${{ github.action_path }}"], check=True)
59|                else:
60|                    run(["uv", "pip", "install", "--python", context.env_exe, r"${{ github.action_path }}"], check=True)
61|
62|
63|        print("::group::Install nox")
64|        nox_bin_path = Path(r"${{ runner.temp }}") / "nox"
65|        if nox_bin_path.exists():
66|            shutil.rmtree(nox_bin_path)
67|        venv_path = Path(r"${{ runner.temp }}") / "nox-venv"
68|        if venv_path.exists():
69|            shutil.rmtree(venv_path)
70|        builder = EnvBuilder()
71|        builder.create(venv_path)
72|        nox_path = [path for path in builder.bin_path.glob("nox*") if path.stem == "nox"][0]
73|        nox_bin_path.mkdir()
74|        try:
75|            os.symlink(nox_path, nox_bin_path / nox_path.name)
76|        except OSError:
77|            shutil.copyfile(nox_path, nox_bin_path / nox_path.name)
78|        with open(os.environ["GITHUB_PATH"], "at") as f:
79|            f.write(f"{nox_bin_path}\n")
80|        print("::endgroup::")
81|      shell: "${{ steps.allpython.outputs.python-path }} -u {0}"
--- END FILE: action.yml ---

3|## 2026.10.20
4|
5|Parallel mode no longer prints an "experimental" banner, and sessions can check
6|`session.parallel` to see if they run in a parallel worker. A new `rattler`
7|backend uses py-rattler (install with the `nox[rattler]` extra), so you can
8|request fast conda-style environments in a `/// script` block. Python versions
9|read from classifiers now include free-threaded builds when the free-threading
10|classifier is present, and are deduplicated. A single-argument
11|`@nox.parametrize` now accepts ranges and other iterators, and the `rattler`
12|backend loads config from the default locations. The GitHub Action now
13|defaults to Python 3.11-3.15. This release also fixes several bugs in script
14|mode, option handling, and `tox-to-nox`.

1039|## 2018.8.23
1040|
1041|**Heads up!** This is a very big release for Nox. Please read these release notes thoroughly and reach out to us on GitHub if you run into issues.
1042|
1043|Breaking changes and other important notes:
1044|
1045|* Nox is now published as "nox" on PyPI. This means that Nox is installed via `pip install nox` instead of `nox-automation`. Since the new release makes so many breaking changes, we won't be updating the old `nox-automation` package.
1046|* Nox's configuration file is now called `noxfile.py` instead of `nox.py`.
1047|* Nox no longer supports Python 2.7. You can still create and run Python 2.7 sessions, but Nox itself must be installed using Python 3.5+.
1048|* Nox's behavior has been changed from *declarative*  to *imperative*. Session actions now run immediately. Existing code to setup session virtualenv, such as `session.interpreter` **will break**! Please consult the documentation on how to use `@nox.session(python=[...])` to configure virtualenvs for sessions.
1049|* Nox now uses calver for releases.
1050|* Support for the legacy naming convention (for example, `session_tests`) has been removed.
1051|
1052|Other changes:
1053|
1054|* Update colorlog dependency range.
1055|* Update installation command in contributing. (#101)
1056|* Remove Python 2.x object inheritance. (#109)
1057|* Fix python syntax error on docs. (#111)
1058|* Show additional links on PyPI. (#108)
1059|* Add contributors file. (#113)
1060|* Run sphinx with -W option. (#115)
1061|* Using `os.pathsep` instead of a hardcoded `':'`. (#105)
1062|* Use a configuration file for readthedocs. (#107)
1063|* Add 'py' alias for `nox.session(python=...)`.
1064|* Fix processing of numeric Python versions that specify a patch version.
1065|* Use Black to format code.
1066|* Support invoking Nox using `python -m nox`.
1067|* Produce better error message when sessions can't be found.
1068|* Fix missing links in README.rst.
1069|* Remove usage of future imports.
1070|* Remove usage of six.
1071|* Make session.install a simple alias for session.run.
1072|* Refactor nox.command.Command as nox.command.run, reducing complexity.
1073|* Add list of projects that use Nox.
1074|* Use witchhazel pygments theme.

160|def _patch_run_session_tracking_concurrency(
161|    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
162|) -> dict[str, int]:
163|    """Patch ``_run_session`` with a fake that records peak concurrency.
164|
165|    The returned dict maps each session's envdir (and the ``"total"`` key) to
166|    the largest number of simultaneously-running sessions observed. The fake
167|    sleeps briefly so that sessions submitted together reliably overlap.
168|    """
169|    lock = threading.Lock()
170|    concurrent: dict[str, int] = {}
171|    peak: dict[str, int] = {}
172|
173|    def fake_run_session(
174|        session: SessionRunner,
175|        _global_config: object,
176|        _children: object,
177|        **_kwargs: object,
178|    ) -> tuple[Result, str]:
179|        with lock:
180|            for key in (session.envdir, "total"):
181|                concurrent[key] = concurrent.get(key, 0) + 1
182|                peak[key] = max(peak.get(key, 0), concurrent[key])
183|        time.sleep(0.05)
184|        with lock:
185|            for key in (session.envdir, "total"):
186|                concurrent[key] -= 1
187|        return Result(session, Status.SUCCESS, duration=0.0), ""
188|
189|    monkeypatch.setattr(_parallel, "_run_session", fake_run_session)
190|    return peak

910|            " sys.stdout.buffer.write(b'crlf\\r\\n')"
911|        )

443|    """Enable keyboard interrupts (CTRL-C) on Windows."""
444|    kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

450|def interrupt_process(proc: subprocess.Popen[Any]) -> None:
451|    """Send SIGINT or CTRL_C_EVENT to the process."""
452|    if sys.platform.startswith("win"):
453|        # Disable Ctrl-C so we don't terminate ourselves.
454|        enable_ctrl_c(enabled=False)
455|
456|        # Send the keyboard interrupt to all processes attached to the current
457|        # console session.
458|        os.kill(0, signal.CTRL_C_EVENT)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
459|    else:
460|        proc.send_signal(signal.SIGINT)

463|@pytest.fixture
464|def command_with_keyboard_interrupt(
465|    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, marker: Any
466|) -> None:
467|    """Monkeypatch Popen.communicate to raise KeyboardInterrupt."""
468|    if sys.platform.startswith("win"):
469|        # Enable Ctrl-C because the child inherits the setting from us.
470|        enable_ctrl_c(enabled=True)
471|
472|    communicate = subprocess.Popen.communicate
473|
474|    def wrapper(
475|        proc: subprocess.Popen[Any], *args: Any, **kwargs: Any
476|    ) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
477|        # Raise the interrupt only on the first call, so Nox has a chance to
478|        # shut down the child process subsequently.
479|
480|        if wrapper.firstcall:  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
481|            wrapper.firstcall = False  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
482|
483|            # Give the child time to install its signal handlers.
484|            while not marker.exists():
485|                time.sleep(0.05)
486|
487|            # Send a real keyboard interrupt to the child.
488|            interrupt_process(proc)
489|
490|            # Fake a keyboard interrupt in the parent.
491|            raise KeyboardInterrupt
492|
493|        return communicate(proc, *args, **kwargs)
494|
495|    wrapper.firstcall = True  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
496|
497|    monkeypatch.setattr("subprocess.Popen.communicate", wrapper)

500|def format_program(program: str, marker: Any) -> str:
501|    """Preprocess the Python program run by the child process."""
502|    main = f"""
503|    import time
504|    from pathlib import Path
505|
506|    Path({str(marker)!r}).touch()
507|    time.sleep(3)
508|    """
509|    return dedent(program).format(MAIN=dedent(main))

68|        (
69|            {

71|                "b": (),
72|                "c": (),
73|                "d": ("e",),

87|            {

89|                "b": (),
90|                "c": ("b",),
91|                "d": ("e",),
92|                "e": ("c",),

108|        #     however, the ``dependencies["a"]`` order preference between ``"b"`` and
109|        #     ``"c"`` is ignored because obeying this order preference cannot be done
110|        #     without making the sort non-lazy (here, calling ``"c"`` earlier than is
111|        #     required by one of its dependents (``"h"``) would be non-lazy).
112|        (
113|            {
114|                "a": ("c", "b"),
115|                "b": (),
116|                "c": (),
117|                "d": ("e",),
118|                "e": ("c",),
119|                "f": ("b", "g"),
120|                "g": ("b", "h"),
121|                "h": ("c",),
122|                "0": ("g", "a", "d"),
123|            },
124|            ("b", "c", "h", "g", "a", "e", "d"),
125|        ),
126|    ],
127|)
128|def test_lazy_stable_topo_sort(
129|    dependencies: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]], expected: tuple[str, ...]
130|) -> None:
131|    actual = tuple(lazy_stable_topo_sort(dependencies, "0"))
132|    actual_with_root = tuple(lazy_stable_topo_sort(dependencies, "0", drop_root=False))
133|    assert actual == actual_with_root[:-1] == expected
134|
135|
136|@pytest.mark.parametrize(
137|    ("dependencies", "expected_cycle"),
138|    [
139|        # Note that these cycles are inherent to the dependency graph; they cannot be
140|        # resolved by ignoring the order preference for a pair in ``dependencies[node]``
141|        # for some ``node``.
142|        (
143|            {
144|                "a": ("b",),
145|                "b": ("a",),
146|                "0": ("a",),
147|            },
148|            ("a", "b", "a"),
149|        ),
150|        (
151|            {
152|                "a": ("c", "b"),
153|                "b": (),
154|                "c": ("a", "b"),
155|                "0": ("a",),
156|            },
157|            ("a", "c", "a"),
158|        ),
159|    ],
160|)
161|def test_lazy_stable_topo_sort_CycleError(
162|    dependencies: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]], expected_cycle: tuple[str, ...]
163|) -> None:
164|    with pytest.raises(CycleError) as exc_info:
165|        tuple(lazy_stable_topo_sort(dependencies, "0"))
166|    # While the exact cycle reported is not unique and is an implementation detail, this
167|    # still serves as a regression test for unexpected changes in the implementation's
168|    # behavior.
169|    assert exc_info.value.args[1] == expected_cycle

1|from __future__ import annotations
2|
3|import json
4|import platform
5|import sys
6|
7|
8|def filter_version(version: str) -> str:
9|    """return python 'major.minor'"""
10|
11|    # remove interpreter prefix
12|    if version.startswith("pypy-"):
13|        version_ = version[5:]
14|    elif version.startswith("pypy"):
15|        version_ = version[4:]
16|    elif version.startswith("~"):
17|        version_ = version[1:]
18|    else:
19|        version_ = version
20|
21|    # remove extra specifier e.g. "3.12-dev" => "3.12", "~3.12.0-0" => "3.12"
22|    version_ = version_.split("-")[0]
23|
24|    # Handle free-threaded
25|    free_threaded = version_.endswith("t")
26|    if free_threaded:
27|        version_ = version_[:-1]
28|
29|    version_parts = version_.split(".")
30|    if len(version_parts) < 2:
31|        msg = f"invalid version: {version}"
32|        raise ValueError(msg)
33|    if not version_parts[0].isdigit():
34|        msg = f"invalid major python version: {version}"
35|        raise ValueError(msg)
36|    if not version_parts[1].isdigit():
37|        msg = f"invalid minor python version: {version}"
38|        raise ValueError(msg)
39|    return ".".join(version_parts[:2]) + ("t" if free_threaded else "")
40|
41|
42|def valid_version(version: str) -> bool:
43|    if sys.platform.startswith("win32") and platform.machine().lower() in {
44|        "arm64",
45|        "aarch64",
46|    }:
47|        if version in {"2.7", "3.6", "3.7", "3.8", "3.9", "3.10"}:
48|            return False
49|    return True
50|
51|
52|def setup_action(input_: str, *, self_version: str = "3.12") -> None:
53|    versions = [version.strip() for version in input_.split(",") if version.strip()]
54|
55|    pypy_versions = [version for version in versions if version.startswith("pypy")]
56|    pypy_versions_filtered = [filter_version(version) for version in pypy_versions]
57|    if len(pypy_versions) != len(set(pypy_versions_filtered)):
58|        msg = (
59|            "multiple versions specified for the same 'major.minor' PyPy interpreter:"
60|            f" {pypy_versions}"
61|        )
62|        raise ValueError(msg)
63|
64|    cpython_versions = [version for version in versions if version not in pypy_versions]
65|    cpython_versions_filtered = [
66|        filter_version(version) for version in cpython_versions
67|    ]
68|    if len(cpython_versions) != len(set(cpython_versions_filtered)):
69|        msg = (
70|            "multiple versions specified for the same 'major.minor' CPython"
71|            f" interpreter: {cpython_versions}"
72|        )
73|        raise ValueError(msg)
74|
75|    # cpython shall be installed last because
76|    # other interpreters also define pythonX.Y symlinks.
77|    versions = [v for v in pypy_versions + cpython_versions if valid_version(v)]
78|
79|    # we want to install our own self version last to ease nox set-up
80|    if self_version in cpython_versions_filtered:
81|        index = cpython_versions_filtered.index(self_version)
82|        index = versions.index(cpython_versions[index])
83|        cpython_nox = versions.pop(index)
84|        versions.append(cpython_nox)
85|    else:
86|        # add this to install nox
87|        versions.append(self_version)
88|
89|    print(f"interpreters={json.dumps(versions)}")
90|
91|
92|if __name__ == "__main__":
93|    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
94|        msg = f"invalid arguments: {sys.argv}"
95|        raise AssertionError(msg)
96|    setup_action(sys.argv[1])
